ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p478/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p478/r10.speaker: شمر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p478/r10.claim: Shammar defines an idol as any statue made from common materials and notes that the word can refer to a cross; Arabs set such figures up for worship.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p478/r10.anchor: قال شمر كل تمثال من خشب أو حجارة أو ذهب أو فضة أو نحاس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p478/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p478/r11.speaker: رسول الله
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p478/r11.claim: The Prophet told ʿAdi ibn Hatim to remove the cross from his neck, calling it an idol.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p478/r11.anchor: وقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لعدي بن حاتم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p478/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p478/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p478/r12.claim: The word for idol comes from setting something firmly in place; the related adjective means settled and fixed, and poetry uses it for steadfastness in a covenant.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p478/r12.anchor: واشتقاقه من وثن الشيء أقامه في مكانه وثبت، والواثن المقيم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p503#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p503#2/r1.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p503#2/r1.claim: Ibn Atiyya supplies 'your prescribed duty' as the omitted predicate after 'that'; al-Zamakhshari supplies 'the matter,' a transition into a new topic.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p503#2/r1.anchor: ذلك خبر مبتدأ محذوف قدره ابن عطية فرضكم ذلك أو الواجب ذلك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p503#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p503#2/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p503#2/r2.claim: Other analyses make the demonstrative the topic with an omitted predicate or an object meaning 'comply with that'; Zuhayr's verse offers a comparable rhetorical transition.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p503#2/r2.anchor: وقيل في موضع نصب تقديره امتثلوا ذلك ونظير هذه الإشارة البليغة قول زهير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p503#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p503#2/r3.speaker: الكلبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p503#2/r3.claim: The forbidden sanctities may mean the rites commanded in Hajj.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p503#2/r3.anchor: ويحتمل الخصوص بما يتعلق بالحج وقاله الكلبي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p503#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p503#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p503#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas takes the sanctities as all prohibitions of Hajj, including sexual relations, quarrelling, and hunting.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p503#2/r4.anchor: وعن ابن عباس هي جميع المناهي في الحج

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p503#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p503#2/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p503#2/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd counts five sanctities: the sacred waymark, mosque, House, month, and pilgrim in ihram until release.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p503#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p503#2/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p503#2/r6.claim: The apparent meaning of sanctities is general: anything God forbids violating, including all religious obligations.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p503#2/r6.anchor: والحرمات ما لا يحل هتكه وجميع التكليفات

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p503#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p503#2/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p503#2/r7.claim: The pronoun in 'it is better for him' refers to magnifying the sanctities, which earns nearness to God and reward; khayr means good rather than comparative goodness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p503#2/r7.anchor: وضمير فهو عائد على المصدر المفهوم من قوله ومن يعظم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p503#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p503#2/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p503#2/r8.claim: Permission for livestock responds to pre-Islamic self-imposed bans such as bahīrah and sā'ibah; the exception refers to animals whose prohibition Scripture states.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p503#2/r8.anchor: وأحلت لكم بهيمة الأنعام دفعا لما كانت عليه من تحريم أشياء برأيها كالبحيرة والسائبة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p503#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p503#2/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p503#2/r9.claim: After magnifying God's sanctities, the verse commands avoiding idols and false speech because monotheism and truthfulness are the greatest sanctities; idolatry itself is falsehood.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p503#2/r9.anchor: ولما حث على تعظيم حرمات الله وذكر أن تعظيمها خير لمعظمها عند الله أتبعه الأمر باجتناب الأوثان وقول الزور

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p503#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p503#2/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p503#2/r10.claim: Min may specify the kind of impurity as idols, or mark its source, making idol worship the origin of all corruption and impurity; on the first parse, other impurities are prohibited elsewhere.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p503#2/r10.anchor: ومن في من الأوثان لبيان الجنس

STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r1.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r1.claim: One dating view holds that the surah is Madinan except verses 52–55, which are Makkan.
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r1.anchor: Some say it is Madinan except for vv. 52–55, which are Makkan (IK)

STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r2.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r2.claim: Another dating view holds that the surah is Makkan except verses 19–22, which are Madinan.
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r2.anchor: others say it is Makkan except for vv.19–22, which are from the Madinan period (Q)

STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r3.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r3.claim: Most authorities regard the surah as containing both Makkan and Madinan verses.
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r3.anchor: Most say it is a mix of Makkan and Madinan verses (Q)

STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r4.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r4.claim: A tradition calls the surah remarkable because it came at night and by day, on journeys and at home, in war and peace, and includes abrogating and abrogated as well as clear and allegorical verses.
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r4.anchor: and it has both muḥkam (unambiguous) and mutashābih (symbolic or allegorical) verses (Q)

STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r8.claim: Pilgrimage rites begin with Abraham; their inward meaning is reverence reaching God, rather than sacrificial meat or other physical aspects.
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r8.anchor:
lies in the inner state of reverence(
taqwā) that reaches God, not sacrificial meat or other physical aspects of the ḥajj

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p163/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p163/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p163/r8.claim: This passage explains the true objective of Abraham's religion and the building of God's House.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p163/r8.anchor: The real objective of Abraham’s (sws) religion and of building the House of God is explained.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:25/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:25/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:25/r1.claim: The passage presents the Sacred Mosque as a universal center, then discusses Abraham's placement at the Kaaba, the call and benefits of pilgrimage, vows, and sacrifice.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:25/r1.anchor: bu âyetlerde Mescid-i Harâm’ın insanlık için önemli bir merkez olduğu belirtildikten sonra Hz. İbrâhim’in “beyt”in (Kâbe) bulunduğu yere yerleştirilmesinden

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:25/r54.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:25/r54.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:25/r54.claim: The clause about avoiding impurity is interpreted either as avoiding idols or as not obeying Satan through idol worship.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:25/r54.anchor: “Öyleyse pislikten yani putlardan uzak durunuz” şeklinde çevirdiğimiz kısmına, “Öyleyse putlara taparak şeytana uymayınız” anlamı da verilmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:25/r55.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:25/r55.speaker: İbn Âşûr
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:25/r55.claim: Ibn Ashur supports interpreting the impurity as idols.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:25/r55.anchor: birinci mânayı destekleyen izah için bk. İbn Âşûr

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:25/r56.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:25/r56.speaker: Taberî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:25/r56.claim: Tabari supports interpreting the clause as not obeying Satan by worshipping idols.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:25/r56.anchor: ikinci mânayı destekleyen izah için bk. Taberî

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:25/r57.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:25/r57.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:25/r57.claim: Calling for avoidance of false speech indicates both that associating partners with God is slander against Him and that lying is a major sin.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:25/r57.anchor: Allah’a ortak koşmanın Allah’a iftira anlamına geldiği, diğer taraftan yalan söylemenin büyük günahlardan olduğu belirtilmiş olmaktadır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:25/r58.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:25/r58.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:25/r58.claim: The Quran repeatedly condemns lying, especially fabricated claims about God; falsehood is called the mother of evils because it conceals wrongdoing and encourages further evil.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:25/r58.anchor: anılan asılsız söz söyleme veya yalan, İslâm ahlâk kültüründeki ifadesiyle “ümmü’l-habâis” yani bütün kötülüklerin anasıdır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:25/r59.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:25/r59.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:25/r59.claim: Scholars allow knowingly lying only in three cases based on a prophetic hadith: defeating an enemy in war, reconciling people, and saving a family about to break apart.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:25/r59.anchor: İslâm âlimleri Hz. Peygamber’in bir hadisine dayanarak (Tirmizî, “Birr”, 26; Müsned, VI, 459-461), sadece şu üç durumda bilerek yalan söylemeyi câiz görmüşlerdir: Savaşta düşmanı yenmek için; insanların arasını düzeltmek ve barıştırmak için; yıkılmak üzere olan bir aileyi kurtarmak için

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:25/r60.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:25/r60.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:25/r60.claim: The commentary points to 25:72 regarding false testimony, 5:1 for the meaning of an'am, and 2:173 for forbidden animal meats.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:25/r60.anchor: yalan şahitliği hakkında bk. Furkan 25/72; bu âyette geçen “en‘âm” kelimesinin anlamı için bk. Mâide 5/1; yasak olduğu bildirilen hayvan etleri hakkında bilgi için bk. Bakara 2/173

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p198/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p198/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p198/r1.claim: The demonstrative summarizes a whole preceding statement: Abraham was informed of Hajj rites, which hearers must heed; it warns them and marks the end of Abraham's directives before addressing their negligent claimed heirs.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p198/r1.anchor: it actually is a substitute of a whole sentence.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p198/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p198/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p198/r4.claim: Idolaters' rules dividing animals into permitted and prohibited categories, including by sex or use as transport, lack any basis in Abraham's religion; only Qur'anic prohibitions apply.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p198/r4.anchor: only those beasts are prohibited which are being recited out in the Qur’ān.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p402/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p402/r1.speaker: هبة الله بن سلامة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p402/r1.claim: His classification places the Meccan portion from the start of verse 30 through the surah's end, and the Medinan portion from verse 25 to the start of verse 30.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p402/r1.anchor: فأما المكي فمن رأس الثلاثين منها إلى آخرها واماالمدني فمن رأس خمس وعشرين إلى رأس ثلاثين

TABATABAI:22:25-37#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:25-37#2/r5.speaker: أصحابنا
TABATABAI:22:25-37#2/r5.claim: The author’s companions report that avoiding the filth of idols includes chess, backgammon, and other kinds of gambling.
TABATABAI:22:25-37#2/r5.anchor: أن اللعب بالشطرنج والنرد وسائر أنواع القمار من ذلك

TABATABAI:22:25-37#2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:25-37#2/r6.speaker: أصحابنا
TABATABAI:22:25-37#2/r6.claim: The author’s companions report that avoiding false speech includes singing and other distracting or frivolous speech.
TABATABAI:22:25-37#2/r6.anchor: أنه يدخل فيه الغناء وسائر الأقوال الملهبة

TABATABAI:22:25-37#2/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:25-37#2/r7.speaker: أيمن بن خزيم
TABATABAI:22:25-37#2/r7.claim: Ayman ibn Khuzaym reports that the Prophet equated false testimony with associating partners with God and recited the command to avoid idol filth and false speech; the author notes this report also appears in al-Durr al-Manthūr.
TABATABAI:22:25-37#2/r7.anchor: عدلت شهادة الزور بالشرك بالله ثم قرأ { فاجتنبوا الرجس من الأوثان واجتنبوا قول الزور }

SAMIN-DURR:22:30/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:30/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:22:30/r1.claim: The preferred parse makes ذلك the predicate of an omitted subject meaning this is the matter or situation.
SAMIN-DURR:22:30/r1.anchor: خبر مبتدأ مضمر أي: الأمر والشأن ذلك.

SAMIN-DURR:22:30/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:30/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:22:30/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari compares this transition to a writer who opens a subject, then resumes with this is how matters stood before turning to another subject.
SAMIN-DURR:22:30/r2.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " كما يقدم الكاتب جملة من كتابه في بعض المعاني، ثم إذا أراد الخوض في معنى آخر

SAMIN-DURR:22:30/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:30/r3.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:22:30/r3.claim: Ibn Atiyya estimates either your prescribed obligation is that or the obligation is that.
SAMIN-DURR:22:30/r3.anchor: وقدره ابن عطية: " فرضكم ذلك، أو الواجب ذلك ".

SAMIN-DURR:22:30/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:30/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:22:30/r4.claim: Other parses make ذلك a subject with an omitted predicate meaning the matter already mentioned, or an accusative command to comply with it.
SAMIN-DURR:22:30/r4.anchor: وقيل: هو مبتدأ خبره محذوف. أي: ذلك الأمر الذي ذكرته. وقيل: في محل نصب

SAMIN-DURR:22:30/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:30/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:22:30/r5.claim: A line by Zuhayr after earlier praise of Haram ibn Sinan offers a poetic example of this transitional هذا.
SAMIN-DURR:22:30/r5.anchor: ونظير هذه الإشارة قول زهير، بعد تقدم جمل في وصف هرم ابن سنان:

SAMIN-DURR:22:30/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:30/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:22:30/r6.claim: هو is a pronoun referring to the verbal noun understood from يعظم: revering God's sacred things is better for the reverer.
SAMIN-DURR:22:30/r6.anchor: ضمير المصدر المفهوم من قوله { ومن يعظم } أي: وتعظيمه حرمات الله خير له كقوله تعالى:

SAMIN-DURR:22:30/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:30/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:22:30/r7.claim: خير has the apparent comparative sense, subject to the familiar interpretive qualification.
SAMIN-DURR:22:30/r7.anchor: و " خير " هنا ظاهرها التفضيل بالتأويل المعروف.

SAMIN-DURR:22:30/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:30/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:22:30/r8.claim: The exception can be connected, referring to livestock made forbidden by an incidental cause such as death.
SAMIN-DURR:22:30/r8.anchor: يجوز أن يكون استثناء متصلا، ويصرف إلى ما يحرم من بهيمة الأنعام لسبب عارض

SAMIN-DURR:22:30/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:30/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:22:30/r9.claim: Alternatively, it is disconnected because no livestock animal is intrinsically forbidden; the author notes the argument was given at the beginning of al-Maida.
SAMIN-DURR:22:30/r9.anchor: وأن يكون استثناء منقطعا؛ إذ ليس فيها محرم وقد تقدم تقرير هذا الوجه أول المائدة.

SAMIN-DURR:22:30#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:30#2/r1.speaker: المعربون
SAMIN-DURR:22:30#2/r1.claim: The commonly held parse takes من as explanatory of kind: avoid the impurity that is idols.
SAMIN-DURR:22:30#2/r1.anchor: أحدها: أنها لبيان الجنس، وهو مشهور قول المعربين، ويتقدر بقولك: الرجس الذي هو الأوثان.

SAMIN-DURR:22:30#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:30#2/r2.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:22:30#2/r2.claim: Abu al-Baqa conflates the explanatory and source meanings, suggesting the first amounts here to the second; the author says it does not.
SAMIN-DURR:22:30#2/r2.anchor: وقد خلط أبو البقاء القولين فجعلهما قولا واحدا فقال: " ومن لبيان الجنس أي: اجتنبوا الرجس

SAMIN-DURR:22:30#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:30#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:22:30#2/r3.claim: من may indicate a starting point or may be partitive.
SAMIN-DURR:22:30#2/r3.anchor: والثاني: أنها لابتداء الغاية. وقد خلط أبو البقاء القولين

SAMIN-DURR:22:30#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:30#2/r4.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:22:30#2/r4.claim: Ibn Atiyya says the partitive reading reverses and corrupts the verse's meaning.
SAMIN-DURR:22:30#2/r4.anchor: وقد غلط ابن عطية القائل بكون

SAMIN-DURR:22:30#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:30#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس وابن جريج
SAMIN-DURR:22:30#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas and Ibn Jurayj allow the partitive reading by taking الرجس as idol worship, the forbidden aspect of idols; the author calls this an unlikely interpretation.
SAMIN-DURR:22:30#2/r5.anchor: وقد يمكن التبعيض فيها: بأن يعني بالرجس عبادة الأوثان. وبه قال ابن عباس وابن جريج،

ZAJJAJ:v3p424/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p424/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p424/r8.claim: God's sacred ordinances include Hajj, ʿUmra, all rites, and every divine obligation; a ḥurma must be upheld and may not be abandoned or neglected.
ZAJJAJ:v3p424/r8.anchor: وحرمات الله الحج والعمرة وسائر المناسك، وكل ما فرض الله فهو من حرمات الله

ZAJJAJ:v3p424/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p424/r9.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p424/r9.claim: ذلك is nominative; the sense is, The command is as stated.

ZAJJAJ:v3p424#2/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p424#2/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p424#2/r1.claim: ما is accusative and refers to the forbidden carrion, blood, strangled and beaten animals, and other prohibitions recited to them.
ZAJJAJ:v3p424#2/r1.anchor: في موضع نصب أي إلا ما يتلى عليكم من الميتة والدم والمنخنقة

ZAJJAJ:v3p424#2/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p424#2/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p424#2/r2.claim: من specifies a species: avoid the abomination that is an idol.
ZAJJAJ:v3p424#2/r2.anchor: ههنا لتخليص جنس من أجناس. المعنى فاجتنبوا الرجس الذي هو وثن

ZAJJAJ:v3p424#2/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p424#2/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p424#2/r3.claim: زور means lying; it may also mean associating partners with God or giving false testimony, and all three explanations are sound.
ZAJJAJ:v3p424#2/r3.anchor: الزور الكذب، وقيل إنه ههنا الشرك بالله، وقيل أيضا شهادة الزور. وهذا كله جائز.

ZAJJAJ:v3p424#2/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p424#2/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p424#2/r4.claim: The verse rebukes idolaters for inventing forbidden categories for livestock, such as reserving unborn animals for men or declaring bahīra and sāʾiba; God alone determines lawful and forbidden food, and fabrication against Him is falsehood.
ZAJJAJ:v3p424#2/r4.anchor: والآية تدل - والله أعلم - على أنهم نهوا أن يحرموا ما حرم أصحاب الأوثان نحو قولهم:

ASAD-NOTES:22:29/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:22:29/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:22:29/r2.claim: Honouring God's sacred commands benefits the worshipper; cattle are lawful except what God specifies as forbidden.
ASAD-NOTES:22:29/r2.anchor: if one honours God's sacred commandments, it will redound to his own good in his Sustainer's sight.

ASAD-NOTES:22:29/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:22:29/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:22:29/r3.claim: The passage commands avoidance of idolatrous practices and every untrue word, and likens associating divinity with anything beside God to a catastrophic fall.
ASAD-NOTES:22:29/r3.anchor: Shun, then, [all that God has forbidden and, most of all,] the loathsome evil of idolatrous beliefs and practices; [45]

ASAD-NOTES:22:29#n44/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:22:29#n44/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:22:29#n44/r1.claim: The Qur'an's principle is that anything not explicitly forbidden is lawful in itself; Asad refers to 5:3.
ASAD-NOTES:22:29#n44/r1.anchor: Once again, the Qur'an stresses the principle that everything that has not been explicitly forbidden is per se lawful.

ASAD-NOTES:22:29#n45/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:22:29#n45/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:22:29#n45/r1.claim: Awthan means concrete idols, but broadly also covers false beliefs, practices, and values treated as objects of worship; this wider sense leads into the ban on untrue speech.
ASAD-NOTES:22:29#n45/r1.anchor: denotes not merely actual, concrete images of false deities but also, in its widest sense, everything that is associated with false beliefs

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1039/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1039/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1039/r1.claim: Arabic word order can express distinct information about who gave, what was given and to whom; its many grammatical permutations capture distinctions that may be expressed by a single sentence in another language.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1039/r1.anchor: أحياناً عندنا 25 جملة في العربية أو أكثر كل واحدة لها معنى يقابلها جملة واحدة في اللغات الأخرى

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1042/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1042/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1042/r1.claim: In 22:28 and 22:34, general remembrance of God is followed by the specific bahīmat al-anʿām; 22:30 discusses livestock itself, so it simply names al-anʿām. The author calls this a linguistic congruity of general followed by specific.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1042/r1.anchor: خاص بعد عامّ وبهمية الأنعام خاص بعد عامّ

NASHR:v2p451#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p451#2/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p451#2/r1.claim: Supplication after completing the Qurʾān is the most important completion practice and a sunna passed down from earlier generations; a Prophetic report through Ibn Kathīr was cited earlier.
NASHR:v2p451#2/r1.anchor: ومن الأمور المتعلقة بالختم الدعاء عقيب الختم وهو أهمها، وهو سنة تلقاها الخلف عن السلف

NASHR:v2p451#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p451#2/r2.speaker: محمد بن جعفر
NASHR:v2p451#2/r2.claim: A report from Jābir attributes to the Prophet that a Qurʾān reader or compiler receives a prayer answered by God, either hastened in this life or stored for the next; al-Ṭabarānī notes its narrow transmission and unusual chain.
NASHR:v2p451#2/r2.anchor: حدثنا محمد بن جعفر الإمام. حدثنا زكريا بن يحيى بن السكن الطائي

NASHR:v2p451#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p451#2/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p451#2/r3.claim: The author says the narrator is trustworthy if the name is Muqātil ibn Ḥayyān, but otherwise unknown; the remaining narrators are reliable, though al-Muḥāribī also narrates from unknown people.
NASHR:v2p451#2/r3.anchor: مقاتل بن حيان كما قيل فهو ثقة من رجال مسلم وإن يكن غيره فلا نعرفه

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p37#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p37#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p37#2/r1.claim: Qatada identifies the prohibited animals as carrion and any animal over which God’s name was not pronounced.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p37#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله ﴿ إلا ما يتلى عليكم ﴾ قال إلا الميتة وما لم يذكر اسم الله عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r1.claim: The demonstrative ذلك can separate two statements or two aspects of one statement; هذا is more usual, as in the cited Qurʾanic example.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r1.anchor: أي الأمر وهذا وأمثاله من أسماء الإشارة يطلق للفصل بين الكلامين أو بين وجهي كلام واحد

ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r2.claim: Zuhayr's line uses هذا after a description of Hرم's generosity and courage, illustrating the demonstrative's discourse function.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r2.anchor: كقول زهير وقد يتقدم له وصف هرم بالكرم والشجاعة : هذا وليس كمن يعيا بخطبته

ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r3.claim: Here ذلك conveys the matter's grandeur and lofty distance, and serves as a concise transition to what follows, which suits what precedes.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r3.anchor: واختيار ( ذلك ) هنا لدلالته على تعظيم الأمر وبعد منزلته وهو من الإقتضاب القريب من التخلص

ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r4.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r4.claim: One analysis makes ذلك accusative under an omitted verb: obey or follow that.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r4.anchor: وقيل : هو في موضع نصب بفعل محذوف أي امتثلوا ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r5.claim: Ḥurumāt is the plural of ḥurma, anything legally sacrosanct; the broad sense includes all religious duties, including pilgrimage rites, and honoring them means knowing their obligation and acting accordingly.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r5.anchor: جمع حرمة وهو ما يحترم شرعا والمراد بها جميع التكليفات من مناسك الحج وغيرها

ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r6.speaker: جمع
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r6.claim: Some commentators restrict God's sacred things here to the rites He commanded.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r6.anchor: وقال جمع : هي ما أمر به من المناسك

ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the sacred things as all pilgrimage prohibitions: sexual relations, sin, disputation, and hunting; honoring them means not approaching them.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r7.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما هي جميع المناهي في الحج فسوق وجدال وجماع وصيد

ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r8.speaker: ابن زيد
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r8.claim: Ibn Zayd lists five sacred things: al-Mashʿar al-Ḥarām, the Sacred Mosque, the House, the sacred month, and the pilgrim in consecration until release.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r8.anchor: وعن ابن زيد هي خمس المشعر الحرام والمسجد الحرام والبيت الحرام والشهر الحرام

ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r9.claim: The person who honors God's sacred things thereby gains what is better for him at his Lord: reward on the Day of Resurrection.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r9.anchor: أنه يثاب عليه يوم القيامة والتعرض لعنوان الربوبية مع الإضافة

ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r10.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r10.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says خير is apparently not comparative, so no comparison or omitted comparator needs to be supplied.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r10.anchor: وقال أبو حيان : الظاهر أنه ليس المراد به التفضيل فلا يحتاج لتقدير متعلق

ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r11.claim: Calling God the person's Lord, with the possessive reference to that person, honors him and signals the reason for the ruling.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r11.anchor: والتعرض لعنوان الربوبية مع الإضافة إلى ضمير ( من ) لتشريفه والإشعار بعلة الحكم

ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r12.claim: What is permitted is slaughtering and eating livestock, since the animals themselves are not described as legally lawful or forbidden; al-anʿām broadly refers to the eight kinds.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r12.anchor: أي ذبحها وأكلها لأن ذاتها لا توصف بحل وحرمة والمراد بها الأزواج الثمانية على الإطلاق

ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r13.claim: Most commentators take the exception as connected: it excludes livestock forbidden for an incidental reason, such as carrion or an offering dedicated to other than God.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r13.anchor: استثناء متصل كما اختاره الأكثرون منها على أن ( ما ) عبارة عما حرم منها لعارض كالميتة

ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r14.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r14.claim: A disconnected exception is also proposed, taking ما as the prohibitions listed in the verse about forbidden foods, some of which are not livestock.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r14.anchor: وجوز أن يكون الإستثناء منقطعا بناء على أن ( ما ) عبارة عما حرم في قوله سبحانه : ( حرمت عليكم الميتة ) الآية

ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r15.claim: The imperfect verb does not indicate future recitation, since the prohibition verse had already been recited; it may evoke that past scene for emphasis.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r15.anchor: والفعل على الوجهين لم يرد منه الإستقبال لسبق تلاوة آية التحريم وكأن التعبير بالمضارع استحضارا للصورة الماضية

ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r16.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r16.claim: Another explanation takes the imperfect as expressing recurring, ongoing recitation appropriate to the context.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r16.anchor: وقيل : التعبير بالمضارع للدلالة على الإستمرار التجددي المناسب للمقام

ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r17.claim: The livestock clause is parenthetical, reinforcing the preceding command to eat and feed and dispelling the idea that consecration forbids livestock as it forbids game.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r17.anchor: والجملة معترضة مقررة لما قبلها من الأمر بالأكل والإطعام ودافعة لما عسى يتوهم أن الإحرام يحرم ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r18.claim: Al-rijs means impurity, and من is explanatory: the idols themselves are the filth to be shunned.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r18.anchor: أي القذر ( من الأوثان ( أي الذي هو الأوثان على أن من بيانية

ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r19.claim: The generic definite article, alongside ambiguity and specification, and commanding avoidance of the object itself intensify aversion to idol worship.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r19.anchor: وفي تعريف ( الرجس ) بلام الجنس مع الإبهام والتعيين وإيقاع الإجتناب على الذات دون العبادة

ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r20.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r20.claim: Another analysis makes من mark the source: after a general command to avoid impurity, God identifies idols as its source because their worship gathers corruption.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r20.anchor: وقيل : من لابتداء الغاية فكأنه تعالى أمرهم باجتناب الرجس عاما ثم عين سبحانه لهم مبدأه

ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r21.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r21.claim: Al-Baḥr reports from Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn Jurayj a partitive reading: al-rijs is idol worship, one forbidden aspect of an idol, while other uses such as building are not prohibited.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r21.anchor: وفي البحر يمكن أن تكون للتبعيض بأن يعني بالرجس عبادة الأوثان وقد روي ذلك عن ابن عباس وابن جريج

ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r22.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r22.speaker: ابن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r22.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya objects that making من partitive reverses and corrupts the meaning; Al-Ālūsī rejects that objection as misplaced.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r22.anchor: فقول ابن عطية : إن من جعل من للتبعيض قلب المعنى وأفسده ليس في محله انتهى

ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r23.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r23.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r23.claim: Al-Ālūsī finds both the source and partitive readings strained and unnecessary, and signals that a further possibility will follow.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r23.anchor: ولا يخفى ما في كلا الوجهين الإبتداء والتبعيض من التكلف المستغنى عنه

ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r24.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r24.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r24.claim: The ف links the command to avoid idols to the preceding implication that God's sacred things must be observed rather than violated.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p147/r24.anchor: والفاء لترتيب ما بعدها على ما يفيده قوله تعالى : ( ومن يعظم ) الخ من وجوب مراعاة الحرمات

ALUSI-FULL:v17p148/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p148/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p148/r1.claim: The exception makes a smooth transition to avoiding idols and explains why livestock is not restricted to familiar sacrificial animals: none of those are forbidden by an incidental cause.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p148/r1.anchor: وذكر أن بالإستثناء حسن التخلص إلى ذلك وهو السر في عدم حمل النعام على ما ذكر من الضحايا والهدايا

ALUSI-FULL:v17p148/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p148/r2.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v17p148/r2.claim: Another reading makes the command a consequence of livestock being permitted: this great blessing calls for gratitude, not disbelief and association; من is causal, specifying offerings to other than God.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p148/r2.anchor: وقيل : الظاهر أن ما بعد الفاء متسبب عن قوله تعالى : ( أحلت لكم الأنعام ) فإن ذلك نعمة عظيمة تستدعي الشكر

ALUSI-FULL:v17p148/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p148/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p148/r3.claim: That causal reading is supported by the later phrase غير مشركين به, which would otherwise repeat the same idea.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p148/r3.anchor: ويؤيده قوله تعالى : فيما بعد ( غير مشركين به ) فإنه إذا حمل على ما حملوه كان تكرارا

ALUSI-FULL:v17p148/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p148/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p148/r4.claim: Al-Ālūsī objects that livestock's lawful status is a legal ruling, not external evidence for monotheism; he deems the proposed causal link very remote and denying that is obstinate.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p148/r4.anchor: أن إحلال الأنعام وإن كان من النعم العظام إلا أنه من الأمور الشرعية دون الأدلة الخارجية

ALUSI-FULL:v17p148/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p148/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p148/r5.claim: The command broadens from the particular evil of idol worship, the chief falsehood because it alleges divine entitlement, to falsehood generally; it also counters pre-Islamic false bans on animals falsely attributed to God.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p148/r5.anchor: تعميم بعد تخصيص فإن عبادة الأوثان رأس الزور لما فيها من ادعاء الإستحقاق

ALUSI-FULL:v17p148/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p148/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p148/r6.claim: The renewed imperative, instead of coordinating falsehood directly with idol impurity, adds emphasis.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p148/r6.anchor: ولم يعطف قول الزور على الرزجس بل أعاد العامل لمزيد الإعتناء

ALUSI-FULL:v17p148/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p148/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p148/r7.claim: Al-zūr means falsehood in general; its root sense is deviation, since a lie deviates from reality, and the genitive construction is explanatory.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p148/r7.anchor: والمراد من الزور مطلق الكذب وهو الزور بمعنى الإنحراف فإن الكذب منحرف عن الواقع

ALUSI-FULL:v17p148/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p148/r8.speaker: ابن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v17p148/r8.claim: A report from Ibn Masʿūd says the Prophet equated false testimony with associating partners with God three times, then recited this verse; the cited collections are named, but Al-Ālūsī notes a weakness in some chains and no explicit proof of restriction.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p148/r8.anchor: لما أخرج أحمد وأبو داود ابن ماجة والطبراني وغيرهم عن ابن مسعود أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v17p148/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p148/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p148/r9.claim: Al-Ālūsī prefers the general meaning of falsehood: the verse can include false testimony without being restricted to it, and the Prophet's recitation does not prove exclusivity.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p148/r9.anchor: وتعقب بأنه لا نص فيما ذكر من الخبر مع ما في سنده في بعض الطرق من المقال على التخصيص

ALUSI-FULL:v17p148/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p148/r10.speaker: مقاتل
ALUSI-FULL:v17p148/r10.claim: Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmits from Muqātil that قول الزور means spoken shirk, referring to the polytheists' talbiya that claimed a partner belonging to God and owning what He owns.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p148/r10.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن مقاتل أنه قال يعني بقول الزور الشرك بالكلام وذلك أنهم كانوا يطوفون بالبيت

ALUSI-FULL:v17p148/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p148/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p148/r11.claim: Al-Ālūsī calls Muqātil's and other specific readings narrower than the general sense, although they fit the context; some restrict the phrase to polytheists' claims that things are lawful or forbidden.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p148/r11.anchor: وهو قول بالتخصيص ولا يخفى أن التعميم أولى منه وإن لاءم المقام كتخصيص بعضهم ذلك

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p382#3/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p382#3/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p382#3/r1.claim: ‘That’ refers to the deeds of pilgrimage just described.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p382#3/r1.anchor: ذلك} أي: الأمر ذلك، يعني ما ذكر من أعمال الحج

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p382#3/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p382#3/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p382#3/r2.claim: The inviolable things are God’s prohibitions and sins; honoring them means refraining from violating them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p382#3/r2.anchor: ومن يعظم حرمات الله} أي معاصي الله وما نهى عنه، وتعظيمها ترك ملابستها.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p382#3/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p382#3/r3.speaker: الليث
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p382#3/r3.claim: Al-Layth defines God’s inviolable things as matters that may not be violated.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p382#3/r3.anchor: قال الليث: حرمات الله ما لا يحل انتهاكها.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p382#3/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p382#3/r4.speaker: الزجاج
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p382#3/r4.claim: Al-Zajjāj says a ḥurma is something that must be upheld and must not be neglected.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p382#3/r4.anchor: وقال الزجاج: الحرمة ما وجب القيام به وحرم التفريط فيه،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p382#3/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p382#3/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p382#3/r5.claim: Some interpreters take the inviolable things here as the pilgrimage rites, based on the surrounding verses.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p382#3/r5.anchor: وذهب قوم إلى أن معنى الحرمات هاهنا: المناسك، بدلالة ما يتصل بها من الآيات.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p382#3/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p382#3/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p382#3/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd identifies them as the Sacred House, sacred territory, sacred month, Sacred Mosque, and consecration.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p382#3/r6.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: الحرمات هاهنا: البيت الحرام، والبلد الحرام والشهر الحرام، والمسجد الحرام، والإحرام

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p382#3/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p382#3/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p382#3/r7.claim: Honoring the inviolable things is better for a person with God in the afterlife.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p382#3/r7.anchor: فهو خير له عند ربه} أي: تعظيم الحرمات، خير له عند الله في الآخرة.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p383/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p383/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p383/r1.claim: Camels, cattle, and sheep are lawful to eat after slaughter.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p383/r1.anchor: أن تأكلوها إذا ذبحتموها وهي الإبل والبقر والغنم،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p383/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p383/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p383/r2.claim: The exception is the prohibited food listed in 5:3, including carrion and blood.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p383/r2.anchor: إلا ما يتلى عليكم} تحريمه، وهو قوله في سورة المائدة: {حرمت عليكم الميتة والدم}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p383/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p383/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p383/r3.claim: People must avoid worshipping idols and stay away from them because they are filth and a cause of punishment; rijz is synonymous with rajz.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p383/r3.anchor: أي: عبادتها، يقول: كونوا على جانب منها فإنها رجس، أي: سبب الرجس، وهو العذاب، والرجس: بمعنى الرجز.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p383/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p383/r4.speaker: الزجاج
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p383/r4.claim: Al-Zajjāj says min marks a kind or category: avoid idols, which are themselves filth.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p383/r4.anchor: وقال الزجاج: {من} هاهنا للتجنيس أي: اجتنبوا الأوثان التي هي رجس

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p383/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p383/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p383/r5.claim: False speech means lying and slander.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p383/r5.anchor: واجتنبوا قول الزور} يعني: الكذب والبهتان.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p383/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p383/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p383/r6.claim: Ibn Masʿūd identifies false speech as false testimony.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p383/r6.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود: شهادة الزور، وروي أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p383/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p383/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p383/r7.claim: A report says the Prophet preached that false testimony is equivalent to associating partners with God, then recited this verse.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p383/r7.anchor: وروي أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قام خطيبا فقال: "يا أيها الناس عدلت شهادة الزور بالشرك بالله"، ثم قرأ هذه الآية

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p383/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p383/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p383/r8.claim: Another interpretation is the polytheists’ talbiya, which says there is no partner except a partner whom they claim God owns along with what he owns.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p383/r8.anchor: وقيل: هو قول المشركين في تلبيتهم: لبيك لا شريك لك لبيك إلا شريكا هو لك تملكه وما ملك.

BAYDAWI-FULL:22:30/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:30/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:30/r1.claim: The demonstrative stands for an omitted clause, meaning the matter is so; similar wording separates two stretches of discourse.
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:30/r1.anchor: خبر محذوف أي الأمر ذلك وهو وأمثاله تطلق للفصل بين كلامين.

BAYDAWI-FULL:22:30/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:30/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:30/r2.claim: God's inviolate things may mean His rulings and all that must not be violated, or the sanctuary and pilgrimage obligations.
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:30/r2.anchor: أحكامه وسائر ما لا يحل هتكه، أو الحرم وما يتعلق بالحج من التكاليف.

BAYDAWI-FULL:22:30/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:30/r3.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:30/r3.claim: A narrower view identifies the inviolate things as the Kaaba, Sacred Mosque, sacred territory, sacred month and pilgrim in consecration.
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:30/r3.anchor: وقيل الكعبة والمسجد الحرام والبلد الحرام والشهر الحرام والمحرم.

BAYDAWI-FULL:22:30/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:30/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:30/r4.claim: Reverence is better for the person as a reward with his Lord.
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:30/r4.anchor: { فهو خير له } فالتعظيم { خير له }.

BAYDAWI-FULL:22:30/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:30/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:30/r5.claim: Livestock are lawful except what God declared forbidden for an incidental reason, such as carrion or an animal offered to other than God; do not invent bans such as baḥīra and sāʾiba.
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:30/r5.anchor: إلا المتلو عليكم تحريمه، وهو ما حرم منها لعارض

BAYDAWI-FULL:22:30/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:30/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:30/r6.claim: Calling idols impurity to be shunned like filth strongly intensifies the prohibition of revering or worshipping them.
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:30/r6.anchor: اجتنبوا الرجس الذي هو الأوثان كما تجتنب الأنجاس، وهو غاية المبالغة

BAYDAWI-FULL:22:30/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:30/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:30/r7.claim: Avoiding false speech generalizes after the specific prohibition because idol worship is the chief falsehood; the context rebukes pagan practices and false claims about God's law.
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:30/r7.anchor: تعميم بعد تخصيص فإن عبادة الأوثان رأس الزور، كأنه لما حث على تعظيم الحرمات أتبعه ذلك ردا

BAYDAWI-FULL:22:30/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:30/r8.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:30/r8.claim: Another view takes this as false testimony, supported by a Prophetic report equating it with associating partners with God and reciting this verse.

BAYDAWI-FULL:22:30/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:30/r9.speaker: النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:30/r9.claim: The Prophet said false testimony is equivalent to associating partners with God, repeating the comparison three times, then recited this verse.
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:30/r9.anchor: روي أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام قال

BAYDAWI-FULL:22:30/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:30/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:30/r10.claim: Zūr derives from deviation, as ifk derives from turning away; a lie departs from reality.
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:30/r10.anchor: من الزور وهو الانحراف كما أن الإفك من الأفك وهو الصرف

BIQAI-FULL:v5p149/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p149/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p149/r9.claim: That points to the great pilgrimage and its abundant benefits in this life and the next.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p149/r9.anchor: المر الجليل العظيم الكبير المنافع دنيا وأخرى ذلك

BIQAI-FULL:v5p149/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p149/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p149/r10.claim: Allah's sanctities include all matters He commands people to do or leave; honoring them means striving to obey and avoid prohibitions.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p149/r10.anchor: حرمات الله } اي ذي الجلال والإكرام كلها من هذا ومن غيره

BIQAI-FULL:v5p149/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p149/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p149/r11.claim: Revering the sanctities is good for the servant before God and demonstrates the heart's piety; violating them harms the violator.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p149/r11.anchor: تعظيمها من تقوى القلوب , وتعظيمها لجلال الله , وانتهاكها شر عليه عند ربه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p149/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p149/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p149/r12.claim: Camels, cattle, and sheep are lawful except what is recited as forbidden, including carrion, blood, and animals dedicated to other than God.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p149/r12.anchor: وهي الإبل والبقر والغنم كلها { إلا ما يتلى

BIQAI-FULL:v5p149/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p149/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p149/r13.claim: The author contrasts God's rule with pagan custom: pagans forbade such animals as baḥīra and sāʾiba while permitting carrion and blood.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p149/r13.anchor: خلافا للكفار في افترائهم على الله بالتعبد بتحريم الوصيلة والبحيرة والسائبة والحامي وأحلال الميتة والدم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p149#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p149#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p149#2/r1.claim: Idols caused the false rules about sacrificial animals; avoiding the cause means avoiding its consequences, so believers must shun idolatrous filth.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p149#2/r1.anchor: وكان سبب ذلك كله الأوثان , سبب عنه قوله : { فاجتنبوا } أي بغاية الجهد

BIQAI-FULL:v5p149#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p149#2/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v5p149#2/r2.claim: The Prophet equates false testimony with associating partners with God, intensifying the warning against it.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p149#2/r2.anchor: وزاد في تبشيعه وتغليظه إذ عدله - كما قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بالشرك

BIQAI-FULL:v5p149#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p149#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p149#2/r3.claim: Qawl al-zūr is every falsehood and deviation from proof, including shirk, inventing forbidden rules without divine warrant, and permitting what revelation forbids.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p149#2/r3.anchor: وهو الانحراف عن الدليل كالشركالمؤدي غلى لزوم عجز الإله

BIQAI-FULL:v5p149#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p149#2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p149#2/r4.claim: The author contrasts zūr, whose root suggests force and roughness, with ḥanīf, whose root suggests softness and ease; the latter inclines toward proof.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p149#2/r4.anchor: الزور تدور مادته على القوة والوعورة , والحنف - كما مضى في البقرة - على الرقة والسهوله

BIQAI-FULL:v5p149#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p149#2/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p149#2/r5.claim: Being ḥunafāʾ for God means inclining wholly toward Him, whose perfection leaves no defect or deviation in His acts.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p149#2/r5.anchor: { حنفاء لله } أذي له الكمال كله , فلا ميل في شيء من فعله

BIQAI-FULL:v5p149#2/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p149#2/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p149#2/r6.claim: The passage confirms exclusive monotheism: worship is sincerely for God, without associating anything with Him.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p149#2/r6.anchor: أي شيئا من إشراك , بل مخلصين له الدين

DURR-FULL:v6p43/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p43/r3.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v6p43/r3.claim: Mujahid says God's sanctities include Hajj, Umra, and all sins He has forbidden.
DURR-FULL:v6p43/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {ذلك ومن يعظم حرمات الله} قال: الحرمة الحج والعمرة وما نهى الله عنه من معاصيه كلها

DURR-FULL:v6p43/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p43/r4.speaker: عطاء وعكرمة
DURR-FULL:v6p43/r4.claim: Ata and Ikrima gloss God's sanctities as sins.
DURR-FULL:v6p43/r4.anchor: عن عطاء وعكرمة {ذلك ومن يعظم حرمات الله} قالا: المعاصي

DURR-FULL:v6p43/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p43/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
DURR-FULL:v6p43/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd identifies God's sanctities as the Sacred Station, the Kaaba, the Sacred Mosque, and the Sacred Town.
DURR-FULL:v6p43/r5.anchor: عن ابن زيد في قوله {ومن يعظم حرمات الله} قال: الحرمات المشعر الحرام والبيت الحرام والمسجد الحرام والبلد الحرام

DURR-FULL:v6p43/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p43/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v6p43/r6.claim: A report from Ayyash ibn Rabi'a says the community remains well while it honors the sanctuary of Mecca properly, and perishes if it neglects it.
DURR-FULL:v6p43/r6.anchor: عن عياش بن أبي ربيعة المخزومي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: لن تزال هذه الأمة بخير ما عظموا هذه الحرمة حق تعظيمها

DURR-FULL:v6p43/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p43/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p43/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas explains avoiding the filth of idols as avoiding obedience to Satan in idol worship.
DURR-FULL:v6p43/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {فاجتنبوا الرجس من الأوثان} يقول: اجتنبوا طاعة الشيطان في عبادة الأوثان

DURR-FULL:v6p43/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p43/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p43/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas explains false speech as fabrication against God and denial of Him.
DURR-FULL:v6p43/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {فاجتنبوا الرجس من الأوثان} يقول: اجتنبوا طاعة الشيطان في عبادة الأوثان {واجتنبوا قول الزور} يعني الافتراء على الله والتكذيب به

DURR-FULL:v6p43/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p43/r9.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v6p43/r9.claim: Ayman ibn Khuraym reports the Prophet preaching that false testimony is equivalent to associating partners with God, repeated three times, then reciting this verse.
DURR-FULL:v6p43/r9.anchor: عن أيمن بن خريم قال: قام رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم خطيبا فقال: يا أيها الناس عدلت شهادة الزور إشراكا بالله ثلاثا

DURR-FULL:v6p44/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p44/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v6p44/r1.claim: Khuraym ibn Fatik reports the Prophet saying after dawn prayer that false testimony equals associating partners with God three times, then reciting verses 22:30-31.
DURR-FULL:v6p44/r1.anchor: عن خريم بن فاتك الأسدي قال: صلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم صلاة الصبح فلما انصرف قائما قال: عدلت شهادة الزور الإشراك بالله ثلاثا

DURR-FULL:v6p44/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p44/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v6p44/r2.claim: Abu Bakra reports the Prophet naming associating partners with God and disobeying parents among the greatest sins, then sitting up to warn against false speech and testimony, which he repeated until the listeners wished he would stop.
DURR-FULL:v6p44/r2.anchor: عن أبي بكرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ألا أنبئكم بأكبر الكبائر قلنا: بلى يا رسول الله

DURR-FULL:v6p44/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p44/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v6p44/r3.claim: Ibn Masud says false testimony is equivalent to associating partners with God and recites the verse.
DURR-FULL:v6p44/r3.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال: شهادة الزور تعدل بالشرل بالله ثم قرأ {فاجتنبوا الرجس من الأوثان واجتنبوا قول الزور}

DURR-FULL:v6p44/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p44/r4.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v6p44/r4.claim: Mujahid glosses false speech as lying.
DURR-FULL:v6p44/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد {واجتنبوا قول الزور} قال: الكذب

DURR-FULL:v6p44/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p44/r5.speaker: مقاتل
DURR-FULL:v6p44/r5.claim: Maqatil says false speech is spoken shirk, exemplified by the polytheists' circumambulation formula that names a partner whom God owns along with what the partner owns.
DURR-FULL:v6p44/r5.anchor: عن مقاتل {واجتنبوا قول الزور} يعني الشرك بالكلام وذلك أنهم كانوا يطوفون بالبيت فيقولون في تلبيتهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p251/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p251/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p251/r1.claim: The demonstrative marks a break between topics or aspects, drawing attention to what follows; when it cannot serve as predicate, an omitted predicate such as this is a statement is understood.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p251/r1.anchor: اسم الإشارة مستعمل هنا للفصل بين كلامين أو بين وجهين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p251/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p251/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p251/r2.claim: Although this is the more usual transition word, the verse uses the remote demonstrative to signal the elevated rank of the preceding matter.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p251/r2.anchor: وأوثر في الآية اسم إشارة البعيد للدلالة على بعد المنزلة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p251/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p251/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p251/r3.claim: That is a fronted subject with its obvious predicate omitted, understood as a statement or the like; it resembles a writer's transition to a new subject.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p251/r3.anchor: فاسم الإشارة مبتدأ حذف خبره لظهور تقديره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p251/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p251/r4.speaker: زهير
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p251/r4.claim: Zuhayr's verse illustrates the common demonstrative this used to mark a transition; Ibn Ashur also cites Qur'an 38:55.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p251/r4.anchor: وقولل زهير : هذا وليس كمن يعيا بخطبته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p251/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p251/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p251/r5.claim: The sentence about honoring God's sanctities is parenthetical, attached as a new purpose to the account of God establishing Abraham at the House; it turns to preserving the foundations of Islamic monotheism.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p251/r5.anchor: وجملة { ومن يعظم } الخ . . . معترضة عطفا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p251/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p251/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p251/r6.claim: The pronoun he refers to the act of honoring, implied by the verb honor.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p251/r6.anchor: وضمير { فهو } عائد إلى التعظيم المأخوذ

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p251/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p251/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p251/r7.claim: The address shifts to Muslims: Islam preserved the sanctities, and Muslims had performed pilgrimage and lesser pilgrimage before pilgrimage became obligatory, before the conquest of Mecca.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p251/r7.anchor: والكلام موجه إلى المسلمين تنبيها لهم على أن تلك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p251/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p251/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p251/r8.claim: Sanctities are things that must be respected; respect means treating them as sacred by not violating God's commands, and the category includes all pilgrimage rites.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p251/r8.anchor: والحرمات : جمع حرمة بضمتين : وهي ما يجب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p252/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p252/r1.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p252/r1.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam limits the sanctities to five: the Sacred Mosque, House, land, and month, and a person while in consecration.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p252/r1.anchor: وعن زيد بن أسلم : الحرمات خمس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p252/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p252/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p252/r2.claim: Ibn Ashur takes the category more broadly to include sacrificial animals, garlands, the sacred site, and other pilgrimage acts and observances.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p252/r2.anchor: والذي يظهر أن الحرمات يشمل الهدايا والقلائد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p252/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p252/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p252/r3.claim: Permission for livestock follows the mention of livestock and sanctities, invalidating pagan self-imposed bans on animals such as bahira, sa'iba, wasila, and hami described in the Cattle chapter.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p252/r3.anchor: لما ذكر آنفا بهيمة الأنعام وتعظيم حرمات الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p252/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p252/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p252/r4.claim: The exception is for livestock prohibitions recited in Qur'an 6:145 and in the earlier Meccan chapter of the Bee.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p252/r4.anchor: واستثني منه ما يتلى تحريمه في القرآن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p252/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p252/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p252/r5.claim: The present tense being recited covers what had already been recited before this sura and remains recited, as well as later revelation such as the verse denying pagan animal categories.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p252/r5.anchor: وجيء بالمضارع في قوله : إلا ما يتلى عليكم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p252/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p252/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p252/r6.claim: The command to avoid idols is stated as a continuing obligation, like the command to believe in God and His messenger.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p252/r6.anchor: والأمر باجتناب الأوثان مستعمل في طلب الدوام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p252/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p252/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p252/r7.claim: The command to avoid idols is an inserted clarification to avoid what is outside God's sanctities, namely idols.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p252/r7.anchor: وفرع على ذلك جملة معترضة للتصريح بالأمر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p252/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p252/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p252/r8.claim: False speech includes lying about God by labeling permitted things such as blood or meat dedicated to another forbidden, and forbidden things such as bahira and sa'iba lawful.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p252/r8.anchor: واجتناب الكذب على الله بقولهم لبعض المحرمات

BURSEVI:v6p20#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p20#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p20#2/r3.claim: That points back to the prescribed matters from God's placing Abraham through the rites of the Ancient House; the verse gathers commanded and prohibited rulings and separates statements or two aspects of one statement.

BURSEVI:v6p20#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p20#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p20#2/r4.claim: Sacred inviolabilities are things that may not be violated: God's rulings, duties, practices, and the Sacred Kaaba, mosque, precinct, and month, observed by knowing their obligation and acting accordingly.
BURSEVI:v6p20#2/r4.anchor: جمع حرمة وهي ما لا يحل هتكه وهو خرق الستر عما وراءه أي أحكامه وفرائضه

BURSEVI:v6p20#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p20#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p20#2/r5.claim: Reverence benefits its practitioner through reward with God in the afterlife.
BURSEVI:v6p20#2/r5.anchor: فالتعظيم خير له ثوابا عند ربه أي في الآخرة

BURSEVI:v6p20#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p20#2/r6.speaker: ابن الشيخ
BURSEVI:v6p20#2/r6.claim: Ibn al-Shaykh reads with his Lord as a sign of reward stored up because the good comes from obeying God.
BURSEVI:v6p20#2/r6.anchor: قال ابن الشيخ : عند ربه يدل على الثواب المدخر

BURSEVI:v6p20#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p20#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p20#2/r7.claim: Inwardly, revering God's inviolability means avoiding His prohibitions; obedience brings the servant to Paradise, but reverence brings the servant to God, so it surpasses service as a way of nearness.
BURSEVI:v6p20#2/r7.anchor: وفي الآية إشارة إلى أن تعظيم حرمات الله هو تعظيم في ترك ما حرمه الله عليه

BURSEVI:v6p20#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p20#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p20#2/r8.claim: Neglecting service incurs punishment, while violating reverence risks separation; ordinary faults may be forgiven, but breach of inviolability can damage religion and divine oneness.
BURSEVI:v6p20#2/r8.anchor: ترك الخدمة يوجب العقوبة وترك الحرمة يوجب الفرقة

BURSEVI:v6p20#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p20#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p20#3/r1.claim: The livestock are the eight pairs of sheep, goats, camels, and cattle, male and female; horses, mules, and donkeys are excluded.
BURSEVI:v6p20#3/r1.anchor: وهي الأزواج الثمانية على الإطلاق من الضأن اثنين أي الذكر والأنثى ومن المعز اثنين

BURSEVI:v6p20#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p20#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p20#3/r2.claim: The exception refers to livestock prohibited elsewhere, such as carrion and animals dedicated to other than God; it is connected because it excludes livestock prohibited for a contingent reason, as in 5:3.

BURSEVI:v6p20#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p20#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p20#3/r3.claim: The parenthetical clarification confirms the permission to eat and feed livestock and prevents the mistaken belief that consecration makes them forbidden like game; obey God's limits and do not adopt pagan bans or permit what revelation forbids.
BURSEVI:v6p20#3/r3.anchor: والجملة اعتراض جيء به تقريرا لما قبله من الأمر بالأكل والإطعام

BURSEVI:v6p20#4/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p20#4/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p20#4/r1.claim: The filth associated with idols is idol worship itself, to be avoided as one avoids impurities.
BURSEVI:v6p20#4/r1.anchor: الرجس الذي هو الأوثان يعني عبادتها كما يجتنب الأنجاس

BURSEVI:v6p20#4/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p20#4/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p20#4/r2.claim: Rijs means something impure; impurity may be natural, rational, legal, or all three, as with carrion, while wine, gambling, and idols are legally impure.
BURSEVI:v6p20#4/r2.anchor: والرجس يكون على أربعة أوجه إما من حيث الطبع وإما من جهة العقل

BURSEVI:v6p20#4/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p20#4/r3.speaker: المفردات
BURSEVI:v6p20#4/r3.claim: Awthan are stones that were worshipped.
BURSEVI:v6p20#4/r3.anchor: والأوثان وهي جمع وثن وهو حجارة كانت تعبد

BURSEVI:v6p20#4/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p20#4/r4.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v6p20#4/r4.claim: Some distinguish a sanam, made of wood, gold, or silver in human form, from a wathan, which is not so fashioned.
BURSEVI:v6p20#4/r4.anchor: الفرق بينه وبين الصنم أن الصنم هو الذي يؤلف من شجر أو ذهب

BURSEVI:v6p20#4/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p20#4/r5.speaker: الإرشاد
BURSEVI:v6p20#4/r5.claim: The avoidance command follows from revering God's inviolabilities; livestock permission might prompt consumption, so the text then clarifies what must be avoided and culminates with the gravest prohibitions.
BURSEVI:v6p20#4/r5.anchor: قال في "الإرشاد" وقوله : {فاجتنبوا} إلخ مرتب على ما يفيده

BURSEVI:v6p21/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p21/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p21/r1.claim: Avoiding false speech generalizes beyond idol worship, the chief falsehood; polytheists falsely claim idols deserve worship and falsely attribute their animal taboos to God.
BURSEVI:v6p21/r1.anchor: تعميم بعد تخصيص فإن عبادة الأوثان رأس الزور والمشرك يزعم أن الوثن يحق له العبادة

BURSEVI:v6p21/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p21/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p21/r2.claim: The command applies to every kind of false statement and forbids approaching any of it.
BURSEVI:v6p21/r2.anchor: قول الزور كله ولا تقربوا شيئا منه

BURSEVI:v6p21/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p21/r3.speaker: النبي ﷺ
BURSEVI:v6p21/r3.claim: The Prophet equated false testimony with associating partners with God, repeated the statement three times, and recited this verse.
BURSEVI:v6p21/r3.anchor: عدلت شهادة الزور الإشراك بالله تعالى ثلاثا

BURSEVI:v6p21/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p21/r4.speaker: عمر
BURSEVI:v6p21/r4.claim: Umar punished false witnesses with forty lashes, blackened their faces with charcoal, and paraded them through the markets.
BURSEVI:v6p21/r4.anchor: وكان عمر رضي الله عنه يجلد شاهد الزور أربعين جلدة ويسود وجهه بالفحم

BURSEVI:v6p21/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p21/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p21/r5.claim: Zur derives from turning aside, as ifk derives from turning or reversing; falsehood is diverted away from reality.
BURSEVI:v6p21/r5.anchor: والزور من الزور وهو الانحراف كالإفك المأخوذ من الإفك الذي هو القلب

BURSEVI:v6p21/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p21/r6.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v6p21/r6.claim: Inwardly, false speech is any spoken claim unsupported by the heart; making a sincere covenant to seek God and then failing it is also false speech.
BURSEVI:v6p21/r6.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : قول الزور كل قول باللسان مما لا يساعده

BURSEVI:v6p21/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p21/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p21/r7.claim: The Persian verses counsel learning truth from the pure heart, seeking freedom sincerely, keeping faith, bearing blame, and remaining content rather than taking offense.
BURSEVI:v6p21/r7.anchor: طريق صدق بياموز ازآب صافي دل براستي طلب ازادكي جو سرومن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p428#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p428#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p428#2/r1.claim: That refers to the pilgrimage rites just mentioned.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p428#2/r1.anchor: يعني ما ذكر من أعمال الحج ومن يعظم حرمات الله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p428#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p428#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p428#2/r2.claim: Honoring God's sacred limits means avoiding what He forbade during consecration, out of reverence for His command.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p428#2/r2.anchor: فيجتنب ما حرم الله عليه في الإحرام تعظيما لأمر الله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p428#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p428#2/r3.speaker: الليث
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p428#2/r3.claim: A sacred limit is something whose violation is not lawful.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p428#2/r3.anchor: قال الليث الحرمة مالا يحل انتهاكه وقال الزجاج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p428#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p428#2/r4.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p428#2/r4.claim: A sacred limit is something one is obliged to uphold and forbidden to neglect.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p428#2/r4.anchor: وقال الزجاج الحرمة ما وجب القيام به وحرم التفريط فيه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p428#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p428#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p428#2/r5.claim: The benefit of honoring the sacred limits is its reward with the Lord in the afterlife.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p428#2/r5.anchor: فهو يعني التعظيم خير له عند ربه في الآخرة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p428#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p428#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p428#2/r6.claim: The livestock had already been discussed at 5:1.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p428#2/r6.anchor: وقد سبق بيانها المائدة 1 إلا ما يتلى عليكم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p428#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p428#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p428#2/r7.claim: The exception means the animals prohibited in 5:3, such as animals killed by strangling.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p428#2/r7.anchor: تحريمه يعني به ما ذكر في المائدة 3 من المخنقة وغيرها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p428#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p428#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p428#2/r8.claim: Another view allows livestock during consecration except game, which is forbidden then.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p428#2/r8.anchor: وقيل وأحلت لكم الأنعام في حال احرامكم الا ما يتلى عليكم في الصيد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p428#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p428#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p428#2/r9.claim: To shun the abomination is to leave it aside.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p428#2/r9.anchor: فاجتنبوا الرجس أي دعوه جانبا قال الزجاج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p428#2/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p428#2/r10.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p428#2/r10.claim: Here min specifies the kind: shun the abomination that consists of idols.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p428#2/r10.anchor: ومن هاهنا لتخليص جنس من أجناس المعنى فاجتنبوا الرجس الذي هو وثن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p428#2/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p428#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p428#2/r11.claim: The commentary refers readers to its earlier explanation of rijṣ at 5:90.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p428#2/r11.anchor: وقد شرحنا معنى الرجس في المائدة 90

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p428#2/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p428#2/r12.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p428#2/r12.claim: One interpretation of false speech is false testimony.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p428#2/r12.anchor: أحدها شهادة الزور قاله ابن مسعود والثاني الكذب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p428#2/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p428#2/r13.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p428#2/r13.claim: Mujahid interprets false speech as lying.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p428#2/r13.anchor: قاله ابن مسعود والثاني الكذب قاله مجاهد والثالث الشرك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p428#2/r14.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p428#2/r14.speaker: أبو مالك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p428#2/r14.claim: Abu Malik interprets false speech as associating partners with God.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p428#2/r14.anchor: قاله مجاهد والثالث الشرك قاله أبو مالك والرابع أنه قول

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p428#2/r15.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p428#2/r15.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p428#2/r15.claim: Al-Zajjaj identifies it as the polytheists' claims about livestock, declaring some lawful and some forbidden.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p428#2/r15.anchor: والرابع أنه قول المشركين في الأنعام هذا حلال وهذا حرام قاله الزجاج

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p419/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p419/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p419/r1.claim: The opening reference points to the commanded acts of pilgrimage and their great reward.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p419/r1.anchor: يقول تعالى: هذا الذي أمرنا به من الطاعات في أداء المناسك،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p419/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p419/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p419/r2.claim: Magnifying God's sacred limits means avoiding His sins and prohibitions and regarding their violation as grave; doing so earns abundant good and reward, as does avoiding other forbidden acts.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p419/r2.anchor: ومن يجتنب معاصيه ومحارمه ويكون ارتكابها عظيما في نفسه،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p419/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p419/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p419/r3.claim: Mujahid, transmitted by Ibn Jurayj, and Ibn Zayd include Mecca, Hajj, Umrah, and all God's prohibitions among the sacred limits.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p419/r3.anchor: قال ابن جريج: قال مجاهد في قوله: {ذلك ومن يعظم حرمات الله} قال: الحرمة: مكة والحج والعمرة،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p419/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p419/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p419/r4.claim: All livestock are lawful, including animals the Arabs had made taboo as bahira, sa'iba, wasila, or ham.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p419/r4.anchor: أي: أحللنا (2) لكم جميع الأنعام، وما جعل الله من بحيرة، ولا سائبة، ولا وصيلة، ولا حام.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p419/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p419/r5.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p419/r5.claim: The exception refers to the forbidden animals listed in 5:3; Ibn Jarir gives this explanation and transmits it from Qatada.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p419/r5.anchor: قال ذلك ابن جرير، وحكاه عن قتادة.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p419#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p419#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p419#2/r1.claim: Here min clarifies the kind: avoid the impurity that consists of idols.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p419#2/r1.anchor: "من" هاهنا لبيان الجنس، أي: اجتنبوا الرجس الذي هو الأوثان.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p419#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p419#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p419#2/r2.claim: The verse pairs associating partners with God and false speech, including false testimony, as in the prohibition on shirk and speaking about God without knowledge.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p419#2/r2.anchor: وقرن الشرك بالله (4) بقول الزور، كقوله:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p419#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p419#2/r3.speaker: أبو بكرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p419#2/r3.claim: Abu Bakra reports the Prophet listing shirk, disobedience to parents, and false speech or testimony among the gravest sins; the Prophet sat up and repeatedly warned against the last.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p419#2/r3.anchor: وفي الصحيحين عن أبي بكرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p419#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p419#2/r4.speaker: أيمن بن خريم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p419#2/r4.claim: Ayman ibn Khuraym reports that the Prophet equated false testimony with shirk three times and recited this verse.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p419#2/r4.anchor: عن أيمن بن خريم قال: قام رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم خطيبا فقال: "يا أيها الناس، عدلت شهادة الزور إشراكا بالله" ثلاثا، ثم قرأ:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p419#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p419#2/r5.speaker: الترمذي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p419#2/r5.claim: Al-Tirmidhi calls the Ayman report gharīb, known only through Sufyan ibn Ziyad, notes disagreement in its transmission, and says Ayman's hearing from the Prophet is not known.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p419#2/r5.anchor: وهكذا رواه الترمذي، عن أحمد بن منيع، عن مروان بن معاوية، به (1) ثم قال: "غريب، إنما نعرفه من حديث سفيان بن زياد.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p419#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p419#2/r6.speaker: خريم بن فاتك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p419#2/r6.claim: Khuraym ibn Fatīk reports that after dawn prayer the Prophet equated false testimony with shirk and recited this verse together with the next verse.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p419#2/r6.anchor: عن خريم بن فاتك (2) الأسدي قال: صلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم الصبح، فلما انصرف قام قائما فقال:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p419#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p419#2/r7.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p419#2/r7.claim: Ibn Masud says false testimony is equivalent to associating partners with God, then recites the verse.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p419#2/r7.anchor: وقال سفيان الثوري، عن عاصم بن أبي النجود، عن وائل بن ربيعة، عن ابن مسعود أنه قال: تعدل شهادة الزور

JISHUMI:v7p4947/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4947/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4947/r6.claim: اجتناب means keeping distant from something.

JISHUMI:v7p4947/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4947/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4947/r7.claim: The root sense of حنف is inclination; another explanation gives it the sense of uprightness and treats أحنف as an optimistic name.
JISHUMI:v7p4947/r7.anchor: والحنف: أصله الميل، ومنه: الأحنف، قيل: أصله الاستقامة، وسمي الأحنف تفاؤلا

JISHUMI:v7p4947/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4947/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4947/r11.claim: One analysis takes من as indicating the genus, effectively commanding avoidance of idols altogether.
JISHUMI:v7p4947/r11.anchor: و (من) في قوله: (من الأوثان) للجنس لا للتبعيض، كأنه قال

JISHUMI:v7p4947/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4947/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4947/r12.claim: Another grammatical view treats من as an extra particle.

JISHUMI:v7p4947/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4947/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4947/r13.claim: A third view takes من as partitive because impurity encompasses idols and other things.
JISHUMI:v7p4947/r13.anchor: وقيل: (من) للتبعيض؛ لأن الرجس يشتمل على الأوثان وغيرها

JISHUMI:v7p4947/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4947/r14.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v7p4947/r14.claim: The verse was said to have been revealed about polytheists who, in consecration, recited a talbiya naming angels as a partner owned by God.
JISHUMI:v7p4947/r14.anchor: قيل: نزل قوله: (فاجتنبوا الرجس من الأوثان) إلى آخره في ناس من المشركين

JISHUMI:v1p534/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p534/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p534/r8.claim: The first min, in “People of the Book,” marks a category, as in “the impurity of idols.”
JISHUMI:v1p534/r8.anchor: الأولى من أهل الكتاب فهي للتنويع

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p155/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p155/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p155/r1.claim: Dhālika predicates an omitted subject, ‘the matter is this,’ like a writer’s transition to a new topic.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p155/r1.anchor: { ذالك } خبر مبتدأ محذوف ، أي : الأمر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p155/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p155/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p155/r2.claim: A ḥurma cannot be violated; protected obligations may be all divine duties or specifically pilgrimage rites.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p155/r2.anchor: والحرمة : ما لا يحل هتكه . وجميع ما كلفه الله تعالى بهذه الصفة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p155/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p155/r3.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p155/r3.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam lists the Kaaba, Sacred Mosque, territory, sacred month, and pilgrim in consecration among five sanctities.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p155/r3.anchor: وعن زيد بن أسلم : الحرمات خمس

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p155/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p155/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p155/r4.claim: Veneration benefits the person and means knowing sanctities must be respected, protected, and observed.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p155/r4.anchor: أي فالتعظيم خير له . ومعنى التعظيم : العلم بأنها واجبة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p155/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p155/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p155/r5.claim: The exception refers to a recited prohibition, 5:3, not livestock itself; do not forbid lawful animals or permit forbidden ones.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p155/r5.anchor: المتلو لا يستثنى من الأنعام ، ولكن المعنى { إلا ما يتلى عليكم } آية تحريمه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p155/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p155/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p155/r6.claim: The command to shun idols and falsehood follows reverence because monotheism and truth are the greatest sanctities.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p155/r6.anchor: لما حث على تعظيم حرماته وأحمد من يعظمها أتبعه الأمر باجتناب الأوثان

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p155/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p155/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p155/r7.claim: Shirk is falsehood because idolaters claim idols deserve worship; avoid idol worship as the chief falsehood and all false speech.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p155/r7.anchor: لأن المشرك زاعم أن الوثن تحق له العبادة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p155/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p155/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p155/r8.claim: Idols, like wine, gambling, and divining arrows, are called filth by analogy; 5:90 gives avoidance of filth as the reason.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p155/r8.anchor: وسمى الأوثان رجسا وكذلك الخمر والميسر والأزلام

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p155/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p155/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p155/r9.claim: Min al-awthān specifies the otherwise broad term rij’s, like specifying a number as dirhams.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p155/r9.anchor: من الأوثان } بيان للرجس وتمييز له

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p155/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p155/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p155/r10.claim: Zūr is linked to deviation and ifk to turning aside; reported senses include declaring lawful what is forbidden and false testimony.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p155/r10.anchor: والزور والأزورار وهو الانحراف ، كما أن الإفك من أفكه

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p21/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p21/r1.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p21/r1.claim: Al-Kalbi interprets honoring God's sacred limits as performing the prescribed rites.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p21/r1.anchor: أحدهما : أنه فعل ما أمر به من مناسكه , قاله الكلبي .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p21/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p21/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p21/r2.claim: A second view is that honoring the sacred limits means avoiding what is forbidden during pilgrimage consecration.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p21/r2.anchor: والثاني : أنه اجتناب ما نهى عنه في إحرامه .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p21/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p21/r3.speaker: author
