MAWARDI-FULL:v4p21/r3.claim: Al-Mawardi's own broader possibility is to perform and enjoin obedience and avoid and forbid disobedience.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p21/r3.anchor: ويحتمل عندي قولا ثالثا : أن يكون تعظيم حرماته أن يفعل الطاعة ويأمر بها , وينتهي عن المعصية وينهى عنها .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p21/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p21/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p21/r4.claim: One explanation of the exception is the prohibited dead, strangled, beaten, fallen, gored, predator-eaten, and idol-sacrificed animals, except those properly slaughtered.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p21/r4.anchor: أحدهما : إلا ما يتلى عليكم من المنخنقة والموقوذة والمتردية والنطيحة وما أكل السبع إلا ما ذكيتم وما ذبح على النصب .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p21/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p21/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p21/r5.claim: A second explanation is that game is not lawful while you are in pilgrimage consecration.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p21/r5.anchor: والثاني : إلا ما يتلى عليكم غير محلي الصيد وأنتم حرم .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p21/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p21/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p21/r6.claim: One reading takes it as avoiding the impurity associated with idols, namely their worship.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p21/r6.anchor: أحدهما : أي اجتنبوا من الأوثان الرجس , ورجس الأوثان عبادتها

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p21/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p21/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p21/r7.claim: Another reading is to avoid the idols themselves because they are impure.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p21/r7.anchor: الثاني : معناه : فاجتنبوا الأوثان فإنها من الرجس .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p21/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p21/r8.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p21/r8.claim: Yahya ibn Salam interprets false speech as associating partners with God.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p21/r8.anchor: أحدها : الشرك , وهوقول يحيى بن سلام .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p21/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p21/r9.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p21/r9.claim: Mujahid interprets false speech as lying.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p21/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p21/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p21/r10.claim: A third explanation is false testimony.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p21/r10.anchor: والثالث : شهادة الزور . روى أيمن بن محمد أن النبي

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p21/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p21/r11.speaker: أيمن بن محمد
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p21/r11.claim: Ayman ibn Muhammad reports that the Prophet said in a sermon that false testimony is equated twice with associating partners with God, then recited these commands.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p21/r11.anchor: روى أيمن بن محمد أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قام خطيبا فقال : ( أيها الناس عدلت شهادة الزور الشرك بالله مرتين )

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p21/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p21/r12.speaker: النقاش
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p21/r12.claim: Al-Naqqash says false speech refers to the worship of polytheists.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p21/r12.anchor: والرابع : أنها عبادة المشركين , حكاه النقاش .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p21/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p21/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p21/r13.claim: Al-Mawardi's fifth possible meaning is hypocrisy: outward Islam paired with inward falsehood.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p21/r13.anchor: ويحتمل عندي قولا خامسا : أنه النفاق لأنه إسلام في الظاهر زور في الباطن .

MUJAHID:v2p423#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p423#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p423#2/r1.claim: God's sacred things include Mecca, Hajj, Umra, and the sins He has forbidden.
MUJAHID:v2p423#2/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ ومن يعظم حرمات الله ﴾ قال الحرمة مكة والحج والعمرة وما نهى الله عنه من معاصيه

MUJAHID:v2p423#2/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p423#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p423#2/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ واجتنبوا قول الزور ﴾ يعني الكذب

MUQATIL:22:30/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:22:30/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:22:30/r1.claim: God's sacred prohibitions here mean all the rites of pilgrimage; honoring them benefits a person in the afterlife.
MUQATIL:22:30/r1.anchor: يعنى أمر المناسك كلها { فهو خير له عند ربه } فى الآخرة

MUQATIL:22:30/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:22:30/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:22:30/r2.claim: The livestock made lawful are the animals that polytheists had dedicated to idols, as discussed in 6:138.
MUQATIL:22:30/r2.anchor: بهيمة { الأنعام } التى حرموا للآلهة فى سورة الأنعام

MUQATIL:22:30/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:22:30/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:22:30/r3.claim: The exception points to the prohibitions recited at the beginning of 5:3.
MUQATIL:22:30/r3.anchor: { إلا ما يتلى عليكم } من التحريم فى أول سورة المائدة

MUQATIL:22:30/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:22:30/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:22:30/r4.claim: The phrase has fronting and means to avoid worshipping the idols Lat, Uzza, and Manat.
MUQATIL:22:30/r4.anchor: { فاجتنبوا الرجس من الأوثان } فيها تقديم يقول: اتقوا عبادة اللات والعزى ومناة

MUQATIL:22:30/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:22:30/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:22:30/r5.claim: False speech means lying, which is shirk.
MUQATIL:22:30/r5.anchor: { واجتنبوا قول الزور } [آية: 30] يقول: اتقوا الكذب، وهو الشرك

MUQATIL:22:30/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:22:30/r6.speaker: محمد بن على
MUQATIL:22:30/r6.claim: Muhammad b. Ali explains false speech as the polytheistic talbiya of Quraysh, Khuza'a, Kinana, and Amir b. Sa'sa'a, who excepted a partner owned by God and meant the angels they worshipped.
MUQATIL:22:30/r6.anchor: عن مقاتل، عن محمد بن على، فى قوله تعالى: { واجتنبوا قول الزور } قال: الكذب وهو الشرك فى التلبية

MUQATIL:22:30/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:22:30/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:22:30/r7.claim: In pre-Islamic pilgrimage, Yemenites called themselves the servants of Akk and asked to make pilgrimage again on riding camels.
MUQATIL:22:30/r7.anchor: وكان أهل اليمن فى الجاهلية يقولون فى التلبية: نحن عرابا عك عك إليك عانية

MUQATIL:22:30/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:22:30/r8.speaker: author
MUQATIL:22:30/r8.claim: Tamim's talbiya mentioned the day's toil, night travel, cold, and heat, saying it did not avoid or harm anything and that the pilgrimage was for a generous Lord.
MUQATIL:22:30/r8.anchor: وكانت تميم تقول في إحرامها: لبيك ما نهارنا نجره، إدلاجه وبرده وحره

MUQATIL:22:30/r9.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:22:30/r9.speaker: author
MUQATIL:22:30/r9.claim: Rabi'a declared a true pilgrimage in worship and servitude, denying that they came for mourning or profit.
MUQATIL:22:30/r9.anchor: لم نأتك للمناحة، ولا حبا للرباحة.

MUQATIL:22:30/r10.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:22:30/r10.speaker: author
MUQATIL:22:30/r10.claim: Qays Aylan's talbiya included an appeal framed around Bakr and the Banu Aghyar.
MUQATIL:22:30/r10.anchor: وكانت قيس عيلان تقول: لبيك لولا أن بكرا دونكا، بنو أغيار وهم يلونكا

MUQATIL:22:30/r11.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:22:30/r11.speaker: author
MUQATIL:22:30/r11.claim: Jurhum's talbiya claimed they were God's servants and ancient stock, had settled His land, were first to keep His covenant, opposed His enemies, and would uphold religion in the valley.
MUQATIL:22:30/r11.anchor: والناس طرف وهم تلادك، وهم لعمرى عمروا بلادك

MUQATIL:22:30/r12.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:22:30/r12.speaker: author
MUQATIL:22:30/r12.claim: Quda'a invoked God as Lord of the sacred and unrestricted territories and asked for mercy as its people came walking.
MUQATIL:22:30/r12.anchor: ارحم مقام عبد وآم، أتوك يمشون على الأقدام.

MUQATIL:22:30/r13.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:22:30/r13.speaker: author
MUQATIL:22:30/r13.claim: Asad and Ghatafan used a Yemeni-style chant about a camel running toward God, its load and unborn foal, and opposition to Christianity.
MUQATIL:22:30/r13.anchor: وكانت أسد وغطفان تقول فى إحرامها بشعر اليمن: لبيك، إليك تعدوا قلقا وضينها

MUQATIL:22:30/r14.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:22:30/r14.speaker: author
MUQATIL:22:30/r14.claim: Some women circled the Kaaba naked at night; another account says they did so by day wearing only the edge of a garment and reciting a verse about exposed parts and gazing on them.
MUQATIL:22:30/r14.anchor: وكانت النساء تطفن بالليل عراة، وقال بعضهم: لا بل نهارا تأخذ إحداهن حاشية برد

MUQATIL:22:30#2/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:22:30#2/r1.speaker: آدم
MUQATIL:22:30#2/r1.claim: Adam's talbiya said he was God's servant, created by God's hands, honored and brought near, and affirmed God as Lord of the House.
MUQATIL:22:30#2/r1.anchor: وكانت تلبية آدم، عليه السلام: لبيك الله لبيك عبد خلقته بيديك

MUQATIL:22:30#2/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:22:30#2/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:22:30#2/r2.claim: The command to avoid false speech means to avoid lying and the shirk uttered during ihram.
MUQATIL:22:30#2/r2.anchor: فأنزل الله عز وجل: { واجتنبوا قول الزور } يعنى الكذب، وهو الشرك فى الإحرام

NASAFI-FULL:v3p103/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p103/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p103/r1.claim: The pilgrim crosses the earth in stages, but seeing the House only deepens longing; touching the Stone does not satisfy it, and yearning sends him circling back.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p103/r1.anchor: جعل يقطع مناكب الأرض مراحل ويتخذ مسالك المهالك منازل فاذا عاين البيت لم يزده التسلى به الا اشتياقا

NASAFI-FULL:v3p103/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p103/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p103/r2.claim: He presents the three obligatory rites of Hajj as a spiritual journey: ihram binds one to Islam, while standing at Arafat expresses supplication and detachment from reliance on deeds and spiritual states.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p103/r2.anchor: وطواف الزيارة آخره فرائض الحج الثلاث وأولها الاحرام وهو عقد الالتزام يشبه الاعتصام بعروة الاسلام

NASAFI-FULL:v3p103#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p103#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p103#2/r1.claim: “That” has an omitted predicate: either “the matter is that” or “let them do that.”
NASAFI-FULL:v3p103#2/r1.anchor: خبر مبتدأ محذوف أى الأمر ذلك أو تقديره ليفعلوا ذلك

NASAFI-FULL:v3p103#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p103#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p103#2/r2.claim: A sacred inviolability is anything that may not be violated; this can mean all divine obligations or specifically the rites of Hajj.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p103#2/r2.anchor: الحرمة ما لا يحل هنكه وجميع ما كلفه الله عز وجل بهذه الصفة من مناسك الحج وغيرهما فيحتمل أن يكون عاما

NASAFI-FULL:v3p103#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p103#2/r3.speaker: قيل
NASAFI-FULL:v3p103#2/r3.claim: One reported interpretation identifies God’s sacred things as the Sacred House, Sacred Site, sacred month, sacred land, and Sacred Mosque.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p103#2/r3.anchor: وقيل حرمات الله البيت الحرام والمشعر الحرام والشهر الحرام والبلد الحرام والمسجد الحرام

NASAFI-FULL:v3p103#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p103#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p103#2/r4.claim: Venerating God’s sacred things is better for the person before his Lord; veneration means recognizing that they must be observed and preserved.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p103#2/r4.anchor: ومعنى التعظيم العلم بأنها واجبة المراعاة والحفظ والقيام بمراعاتها

NASAFI-FULL:v3p103#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p103#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p103#2/r5.claim: All livestock are lawful except what the Quran specifically excludes; people must respect its limits, neither banning lawful animals as with the bahīra nor permitting carrion or animals killed by strangling.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p103#2/r5.anchor: ﴿ إلا ما يتلى عليكم ﴾ آية تحريمه وذلك قوله حرمت عليكم الميتة الآية

NASAFI-FULL:v3p103#2/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p103#2/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p103#2/r6.claim: The command to avoid idols and false speech follows the exhortation to honor God’s sacred things because these are among the gravest violations.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p103#2/r6.anchor: ولما حث على تعظيم حرماته أتبعه الامر باجتناب الاوثان وقول الزور

NASAFI-FULL:v3p103#2/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p103#2/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p103#2/r7.claim: “From idols” explains the otherwise unspecified “abomination,” as if the text said to avoid the abomination that is idols.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p103#2/r7.anchor: ومن الاوثان بيان للرجس مبهم يتناول غير شئ كانه قيل فاجتنبوا الرجس الذى هو الاوثان

NASAFI-FULL:v3p103#2/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p103#2/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p103#2/r8.claim: Idols are called an abomination by comparison: people naturally recoil from filth and should recoil from idols in the same way.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p103#2/r8.anchor: وسمى الأوثان رجسا على طريقة التشبيه يعنى أنكم تنفرون بطباعكم عن الرجس فعليكم أن تنفروا عنها

NASAFI-FULL:v3p103#2/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p103#2/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p103#2/r9.claim: False speech may mean lies and slander or false testimony; shirk is also falsehood because the idolater wrongly claims an idol deserves worship.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p103#2/r9.anchor: أى الكذب والبهتان أو شهادة الزور وهو من الزور وهو الانحراف لأن الشرك من باب الزور

QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r1.claim: “That” can be nominative, with an implied “your obligation is that,” or accusative, with an implied command to carry it out.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r1.anchor: بتقدير: فرضكم ذلك، أو الواجب ذلك

QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r2.claim: The demonstrative is an eloquent pointing expression, comparable to the wording in Zuhayr's verse.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r2.anchor: ونحو هذه الإشارة البليغة قول زهير

QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r3.claim: The sacred matters first refer to pilgrimage rites mentioned in 22:29; veneration of sacred places is included, according to Ibn Zayd and others.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r3.anchor: والحرمات المقصودة هنا هي أفعال الحج المشار إليها

QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r4.claim: Taken together, the sacred matters mean obeying God's commands in obligatory duties and recommended practices.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r4.anchor: الحرمات امتثال الأمر في فرائضه وسننه

QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r5.claim: Revering God's sacred matters benefits a person more than neglecting any of them.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r5.anchor: أي التعظيم خير له عند ربه من التهاون بشيء منها

QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r6.claim: An alternative takes “better” as a promise of good for the person, rather than a comparative.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r6.anchor: وليست للتفضيل وإنما هي عدة بخير

QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r7.claim: The livestock made lawful for eating are camels, cattle, and sheep.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r7.anchor: أن تأكلوها وهي الإبل والبقر والغنم

QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r8.claim: The exception refers to prohibited animals recited in scripture, including carrion, animals killed by blows, and related categories.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r8.anchor: أي في الكتاب من المحرمات وهي الميتة والموقوذة وأخواتها

QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r9.claim: The livestock rule connects with pilgrimage, where sacrifice is offered, by clarifying which animals may be slaughtered and eaten.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r9.anchor: ولهذا اتصال بأمر الحج فإن في الحج الذبح

QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r10.claim: Another interpretation is that the exception excludes game while you are in a state of ihram.

QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r11.claim: Rijs means something filthy; a wathan is an image made of wood, iron, gold, silver, or similar material, which Arabs set up and worship.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r11.anchor: الرجس: الشيء القذر. والوثن: التمثال من خشب أو حديد أو ذهب أو فضة

QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r12.claim: The Christian cross is like an idol because Christians erect, worship, and venerate it.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r12.anchor: والنصارى تنصب الصليب وتعبده وتعظمه فهو كالتمثال أيضا

QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r13.speaker: عدي بن حاتم
QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r13.claim: Adi ibn Hatim reports that when he came to the Prophet wearing a gold cross, the Prophet told him to remove that idol, meaning the cross.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r13.anchor: وقال عدي بن حاتم: أتيت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وفي عنقي صليب من ذهب

QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r14.claim: The word wathan derives from something standing in its place; an idol is named for being fixed upright in one place and not moving away.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r14.anchor: وأصله من وثن الشيء أي أقام في مقامه

QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r15.speaker: ابن عباس وابن جريج
QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r15.claim: Ibn Abbas and Ibn Jurayj explain the command as avoiding the worship of idols.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r15.anchor: يريد اجتنبوا عبادة الأوثان روي عن ابن عباس وابن جريج

QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r16.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r16.claim: Idols are called filth because they cause divine punishment.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r16.anchor: وسماها رجسا لأنها سبب الرجز وهو العذاب

QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r17.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r17.claim: Another view calls idols impure; impurity is a legal status rather than an intrinsic property of objects, and is removed only through faith, just as ritual purification requires water.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r17.anchor: وليست النجاسة وصفا ذاتيا للأعيان وإنما هي وصف شرعي من أحكام الإيمان

QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r18.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r18.claim: The preposition min may explain the kind of filth, restricting this prohibition to idol filth while other filth is forbidden elsewhere.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r18.anchor: قيل: إنها لبيان الجنس، فيقع نهيه عن رجس الأوثان فقط

QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r19.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r19.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r19.claim: Alternatively, min marks the starting point: a general ban on filth begins with idol worship, which gathers every corruption and filth.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r19.anchor: ويحتمل أن تكون لابتداء الغاية فكأنهم نهاهم عن الرجس عاما

QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r20.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r20.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r20.claim: Taking min as partitive reverses and corrupts the verse's meaning.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r20.anchor: ومن قال إن «من» للتبعيض، قلب معنى الآية وأفسده

QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r21.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r21.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r21.claim: Zūr means falsehood and lies; it is so named because it deviates from truth, as in the cave verse's “turning aside” and the name of a slanted city; anything other than truth is falsehood.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31/r21.anchor: والزور: الباطل والكذب. وسمي زورا لأنه أميل عن الحق

QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31#2/r1.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:22:30-31#2/r1.claim: The Prophet is reported to have said in a sermon that false testimony is equivalent to associating partners with God.

QASHANI:22:29-30/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:22:29-30/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:22:29-30/r4.claim: God's sacred rites include what must not be violated, self-offering and purification, and the spiritual practices of virtue, avoiding vice, receiving disclosures, adopting divine attributes, and ascending stations.
QASHANI:22:29-30/r4.anchor: وهي مالا يحل هتكه وتطهيره والقربان بالنفس وجميع ما ذكر من المناسك كالتحلي بالفضائل

QASHANI:22:29-30/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:22:29-30/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:22:29-30/r5.claim: Honoring these sacred things benefits the wayfarer in God's presence and the station of nearness.

QASHANI:22:29-30/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:22:29-30/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:22:29-30/r6.claim: The lawful cattle are sound souls whose moral qualities and deeds may be used along the path, enjoying their rights rather than personal interests.
QASHANI:22:29-30/r6.anchor: أنعام النفوس السليمة بالانتفاع بأخلاقها وأعمالها في الطريقة والتمتع بالحقوق دون الحظوظ

QASHANI:22:29-30/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:22:29-30/r7.speaker: author
QASHANI:22:29-30/r7.claim: The forbidden exceptions are vices that masquerade as virtues: acts issuing from the soul in an improper way, prohibited to spiritual wayfarers.
QASHANI:22:29-30/r7.anchor: في صورة المائدة من الرذائل المشتبهة بالفضائل وهي التي صدرت من النفس لا على وجهها

QASHANI:22:29-30/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:22:29-30/r8.speaker: author
QASHANI:22:29-30/r8.claim: Idols signify enslaving desires and followed whims, as in 45:23.
QASHANI:22:29-30/r8.anchor: أوثان الشهوات المتعبدة؛ والأهواء المتبعة، كقوله تعالى: أفرأيت من اتخذ إلهه هواه

QASHANI:22:29-30/r9.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:22:29-30/r9.speaker: author
QASHANI:22:29-30/r9.claim: False speech signifies embellished sciences and specious doubts built from imaginings and suppositions for disputation and sophistry.
QASHANI:22:29-30/r9.anchor: من العلوم المزخرفة والشبهات المموهة من التخيلات والموهومات، المستعملة في الجدل والخلاف

RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r1.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r1.claim: Al-Kashshaf treats “that” as the predicate of an omitted subject, “the matter is this”; it is a transition like a writer’s phrase when turning to a new topic.
RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r1.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) { ذالك } خبر مبتدأ محذوف أي الأمر والشأن ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r2.claim: A ḥurma is something whose violation is forbidden; God’s sacred ordinances may mean all obligations or specifically those connected with pilgrimage.
RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r2.anchor: والحرمة ما لا يحل هتكه وجميع ما كلفه الله تعالى بهذه الصفة

RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r3.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam lists five sacred things: the Kaaba, Sacred Mosque, Sacred City, sacred month, and sacred site.
RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r3.anchor: وعن زيد بن أسلم الحرمات خمس : الكعبة الحرام والمسجد الحرام والبلد الحرام

RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r4.speaker: المتكلمون
RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r4.claim: The theologians say that supererogatory acts are not included among God’s sacred ordinances.
RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r4.anchor: وقال المتكلمون ولا تدخل النوافل في حرمات الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r5.claim: Honoring God’s sacred ordinances benefits the person because they must be observed and protected; “with his Lord” points to stored reward, not good already received.
RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r5.anchor: أي فالتعظيم خير له للعلم بأنه يجب القيام بمراعاتها وحفظها

RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r6.speaker: الأصم
RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r6.claim: Al-Asamm explains that honoring the sacred ordinances is better than treating them lightly.
RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r6.anchor: قال الأصم فهو خير له من التهاون بذلك

RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r7.claim: Because a pilgrim might suppose that consecration forbids livestock along with game, God clarifies that livestock remains lawful except for the prohibitions recited in the Qur’an.
RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r7.anchor: فقد كان يجوز أن يظن أن الإحرام إذا حرم الصيد وغيره فالأنعام أيضا تحرم

RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r8.claim: After praising respect for sacred ordinances, the verse commands avoiding idols and false speech because monotheism and truthful speech are the greatest good; shirk is itself a form of falsehood.
RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r8.anchor: أتبعه بالأمر باجتناب الأوثان وقول الزور . لأن توحيد الله تعالى وصدق القول أعظم الخيرات

RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r9.claim: The command means avoiding idol worship, the chief form of falsehood, and avoiding every kind of false speech rather than approaching any of it.
RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r9.anchor: فكأنه قال فاجتنبوا عبادة الأوثان التي هي رأس الزور ، واجتنبوا قول الزور كله

RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r10.claim: Calling idols rijz does not mean they are physically impure: avoiding them is more emphatically required than avoiding filth, and their worship is worse than contact with physical impurity.
RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r10.anchor: وسمى الأوثان رجسا لا للنجاسة ، لكن لأن وجوب تجنبها أوكد من وجوب تجنب الرجس

RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r11.speaker: الأصم
RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r11.claim: Al-Asamm says idols were called rijz because people customarily spilled blood over them as offerings; al-Razi calls this explanation far-fetched.
RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r11.anchor: قال الأصم إنما وصفها بذلك لأن عادتهم في المتقربات أن يتعمدوا سقوط الدماء عليها وهذا بعيد

RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r12.claim: Al-Razi prefers the alternative explanation that idols are called rijz to disparage and belittle them.
RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r12.anchor: وقيل إنه إنما وصفها بذلك استحقارا واستخفافا وهذا أقرب

RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r13.claim: “From idols” explains or specifies rijz, like “twenty of dirhams”: because rijz is broad, the phrase means the filth that consists of idols, not that only some idols are rijz.
RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r13.anchor: بيان للرجس وتمييز له كقوله عندي عشرون من الدراهم لأن الرجس لما فيه من الإيهام

RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r14.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r14.claim: Zūr derives from deviation or turning aside, just as ifk derives from turning someone away.
RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r14.anchor: والزور من الزور والإزورار وهو الانحراف ، كما أن الأفك من أفكه إذا صرفه

RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r15.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r15.claim: One interpretation of false speech is the fabricated claim that something is lawful or unlawful.
RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r15.anchor: أحدها : أنه قولهم هذا حلال وهذا حرام وما أشبه ذلك من افترائهم

RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r16.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r16.claim: A report says the Prophet, after the dawn prayer, stood facing the people, declared false testimony equal to associating partners with God, and recited this verse; al-Razi gives no grading.
RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r16.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( أنه صلى الصبح فلما سلم قام قائما

RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r17.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r17.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r17.claim: Other interpretations of false speech are lying and slander.

RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r18.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r18.speaker: أهل الجاهلية
RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r18.claim: The pre-Islamic pilgrimage chant counted as false speech because it affirmed a partner for God while claiming that God owned that partner and whatever it owned.
RAZI-FULL:v23p28#2/r18.anchor: ورابعها : قول أهل الجاهلية في تلبيتهم لبيك لا شريك لك إلا شريك هو لك

STUDYQURAN:22:30/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:22:30/r1.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:22:30/r1.claim: The sacred things are the Hajj, ʿumrah, Makkah and its environs, and indirectly the things prohibited there.
STUDYQURAN:22:30/r1.anchor: The sacred things are the ḥajj, the ʿumrah, Makkah and its environs, and indirectly whatever is prohibited there (Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:22:30/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:22:30/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:22:30/r2.claim: Ḥurumāt can also mean forbidden things, those things that may not be violated; verse 32 applies magnification to rituals.
STUDYQURAN:22:30/r2.anchor: can also be rendered “forbidden things,” meaning those things that cannot be violated

STUDYQURAN:22:30/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:22:30/r3.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:22:30/r3.claim: Permitted cattle means the kinds of animals that may be sacrificed and eaten; the recited exceptions prohibit carrion, blood, pork, and animals consecrated to other than God.
STUDYQURAN:22:30/r3.anchor: Cattle are permitted refers to the different kinds of animals that can be sacrificed and consumed, and save that which is recited unto you indicates the prohibitions in the Quran against carrion, blood, pork, and anything that is consecrated to other than God (Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:22:30/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:22:30/r4.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:22:30/r4.claim: Shunning the filth of idols means refraining from worshipping them.
STUDYQURAN:22:30/r4.anchor: shun the filth of idols by not worshipping them

STUDYQURAN:22:30/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:22:30/r5.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:22:30/r5.claim: Shunning false speech means rejecting claims made about idols, including that they bring people near to God and that God has daughters.
STUDYQURAN:22:30/r5.anchor: false speech by rejecting assertions about the idols, such as We do not worship them, save to bring us nigh in nearness unto God (39:3) and assigning daughters to God (16:57; Ṭ)

QUSHAYRI:v2p318/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p318/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p318/r2.claim: Venerating God’s sacred limits means venerating His command, which is done by avoiding disobedience.
QUSHAYRI:v2p318/r2.anchor: تعظيم الحرمات بتعظيم أمره ؛ وتعظيم أمره بترك مخالفته

QUSHAYRI:v2p318/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p318/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p318/r3.claim: Seeking approval apart from God’s approval brings no blessing; preferring one’s desire to the Master’s approval soon brings its consequence.
QUSHAYRI:v2p318/r3.anchor: من طلب الرضا بغير رضى الله لم يبارك له فيما آثره ومن هواه على رضى مولاه

QUSHAYRI:v2p318/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p318/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p318/r4.claim: One venerates God’s sacred limits by jealous care for faith; no one who violates a sacred trust escapes consequence.
QUSHAYRI:v2p318/r4.anchor: تعظيم حرماته بالغيرة على إيمانه وما فجر صاحب حرمة قط

QUSHAYRI:v2p318/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p318/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p318/r5.claim: Neglecting service brings punishment, while neglecting reverence brings separation from God.
QUSHAYRI:v2p318/r5.anchor: ترك الخدمة يوجب العقوبة ، وترك الحرمة يوجب الفرقة

QUSHAYRI:v2p318/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p318/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p318/r6.claim: Other acts of disobedience may admit forgiveness and hope, but abandoning reverence risks an unforgiven state that can unsettle faith and oneness.
QUSHAYRI:v2p318/r6.anchor: ترك الحرمة على خطر ألا يغفر

QUSHAYRI:v2p318/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p318/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p318/r7.claim: The prohibited livestock include swine, animals strangled to death, and those specified by the revealed law.
QUSHAYRI:v2p318/r7.anchor: فالخنزير من جملة المحرمات كذلك النطيحة والموقوذة ، وما يجيء تفصيله في نص الشرع

QUSHAYRI:v2p318/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p318/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p318/r8.claim: Here مِن marks the genus of idolatrous filth, rather than a part of it.
QUSHAYRI:v2p318/r8.anchor: ( من ) ههاهنا للجنس لا للتبغيض ، وهوى كل من اتبعه معبوده

QUSHAYRI:v2p318/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p318/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p318/r9.claim: Whatever a person follows as desire becomes that person’s object of worship; each person’s idol is the self.
QUSHAYRI:v2p318/r9.anchor: وهوى كل من اتبعه معبوده ، وصنم كل أحد نفسه

QUSHAYRI:v2p318/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p318/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p318/r10.claim: False speech includes a tongue saying what the heart does not support and breaking a covenant made inwardly with God.
QUSHAYRI:v2p318/r10.anchor: ومن جملة ذلك قول اللسان بما لا يساعده قول القلب ونطقه ، ومن عاهد الله بقلبه ثم لا يفي بذلك

QUSHAYRI:v2p318/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p318/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p318/r11.claim: A ḥanīf turns toward truth and away from falsehood in heart and self, publicly and privately, in deeds, states, and words.
QUSHAYRI:v2p318/r11.anchor: الحنيف المائل إلى الحق عن الباطل في القلب والنفس ، في الجهر وفي السر ، في الأفعال وفي الأحوال وفي الأقوال

TAB-FULL:v16p534/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p534/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p534/r1.claim: The word ذلك points to the required pilgrimage acts just mentioned: removing ritual dishevelment, fulfilling vows, and circumambulating the Ancient House.
TAB-FULL:v16p534/r1.anchor: عن ابن جريج، قال: قال مجاهد، في قوله: {ذلك ومن يعظم حرمات الله} [الحج: 30] قال: " الحرمة: مكة والحج والعمرة،

TAB-FULL:v16p534/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p534/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p534/r2.claim: Whoever honors God's boundaries by avoiding what He forbids during consecration, and does not violate His sacred limits, gains good with God in the afterlife.
TAB-FULL:v16p534/r2.anchor: يقول: ومن يجتنب ما أمره الله باجتنابه في حال إحرامه تعظيما منه لحدود الله أن يواقعها، وحرمه أن يستحلها،

TAB-FULL:v16p534/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p534/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v16p534/r3.claim: Mujahid includes Mecca, Hajj, ʿUmra, and all sins God has forbidden among the sacred things.
TAB-FULL:v16p534/r3.anchor: عن ابن جريج، قال: قال مجاهد، في قوله: {ذلك ومن يعظم حرمات الله} [الحج: 30] قال: " الحرمة: مكة والحج والعمرة،

TAB-FULL:v16p534/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p534/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v16p534/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd lists the Sacred Station, Sacred House, Sacred Mosque, and Sacred Land as the inviolable things.
TAB-FULL:v16p534/r4.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {ومن يعظم حرمات الله} [الحج: 30] قال: " الحرمات: المشعر الحرام، والبيت الحرام، والمسجد الحرام،

TAB-FULL:v16p534#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p534#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p534#2/r1.claim: Livestock are lawful to eat after proper slaughter; pre-Islamic categories such as bahira, saʾiba, wasila, hami, and animals dedicated to idols are not thereby forbidden.
TAB-FULL:v16p534#2/r1.anchor: وذلك: الميتة، والدم، ولحم الخنزير، وما أهل لغير الله به،

TAB-FULL:v16p534#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p534#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p534#2/r2.claim: The exception refers to scripture's forbidden foods: carrion, blood, pork, offerings to other than God, strangled, beaten, fallen, gored, predator-eaten animals, and sacrifices on stone altars.
TAB-FULL:v16p534#2/r2.anchor: وذلك: الميتة، والدم، ولحم الخنزير، وما أهل لغير الله به،

TAB-FULL:v16p534#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p534#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v16p534#2/r3.claim: Qatada glosses the exception as carrion and animals over which God's name was not pronounced.
TAB-FULL:v16p534#2/r3.anchor: عن قتادة: {إلا ما يتلى عليكم} [المائدة: 1] قال: «إلا الميتة، وما لم يذكر اسم الله عليه»

TAB-FULL:v16p535/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p535/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p535/r1.claim: The command means to avoid worshiping idols and obeying Satan in their worship, since idolatry is defilement.
TAB-FULL:v16p535/r1.anchor: عن ابن جريج، في قوله: {الرجس من الأوثان} [الحج: 30] قال: «عبادة الأوثان»

TAB-FULL:v16p535/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p535/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v16p535/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says to avoid obeying Satan in worship of idols.
TAB-FULL:v16p535/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {فاجتنبوا الرجس من الأوثان} [الحج: 30] يقول تعالى ذكره: «فاجتنبوا طاعة الشيطان

TAB-FULL:v16p535/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p535/r3.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v16p535/r3.claim: Ibn Jurayj glosses the defilement from idols as worship of idols.
TAB-FULL:v16p535/r3.anchor: عن ابن جريج، في قوله: {الرجس من الأوثان} [الحج: 30] قال: «عبادة الأوثان»

TAB-FULL:v16p535#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p535#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p535#2/r1.claim: Avoid lying and fabricating claims about God, including saying idols only bring people nearer to Him (39:3) or that angels are His daughters; such speech is falsehood and shirk.

TAB-FULL:v16p535#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p535#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v16p535#2/r2.claim: Mujahid glosses قول الزور as lying.

TAB-FULL:v16p535#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p535#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v16p535#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the following wording as fabrication about God and denial.
TAB-FULL:v16p535#2/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس: {واجتنبوا قول الزور حنفاء لله غير مشركين به} [الحج: 31] يعني: «الافتراء على الله، والتكذيب»

TAB-FULL:v16p535#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p535#2/r4.speaker: عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v16p535#2/r4.claim: ʿAbd Allah says false testimony is equivalent to shirk and recites this verse.
TAB-FULL:v16p535#2/r4.anchor: عن عبد الله، قال: «تعدل شهادة الزور بالشرك» وقرأ: {فاجتنبوا الرجس من الأوثان واجتنبوا قول الزور} [الحج: 30]

TAB-FULL:v16p535#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p535#2/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن خريم بن فاتك
TAB-FULL:v16p535#2/r5.claim: Khuraym ibn Fatik reports the Prophet equating false testimony with associating partners with God, then reciting the verse.
TAB-FULL:v16p535#2/r5.anchor: عن خريم بن فاتك، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «عدلت شهادة الزور بالشرك بالله»، ثم قرأ: {فاجتنبوا الرجس من الأوثان واجتنبوا قول الزور} [الحج: 30]

TAB-FULL:v16p535#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p535#2/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن أيمن بن خريم
TAB-FULL:v16p535#2/r6.claim: Ayman ibn Khuraym reports the Prophet twice declaring in a sermon that false testimony is equivalent to shirk, then reciting the verse.
TAB-FULL:v16p535#2/r6.anchor: عن أيمن بن خريم، أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قام خطيبا فقال: «أيها الناس عدلت شهادة الزور بالشرك بالله»

TAB-FULL:v16p535#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p535#2/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p535#2/r7.claim: Al-Tabari rejects the objection that only some idols are defilement: all are, and the phrase means avoiding the defilement that comes from idols, namely worshiping them.
TAB-FULL:v16p535#2/r7.anchor: قيل: كلها رجس. وليس المعنى ما ذهبت إليه في ذلك، وإنما معنى الكلام: فاجتنبوا الرجس الذي يكون من الأوثان، أي: عبادتها

TABATABAI:22:29-30/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:29-30/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:22:29-30/r5.claim: A hurma is what may not be violated and must be observed; awthan are idols, and zawr is deviation from truth, hence lying or false speech.
TABATABAI:22:29-30/r5.anchor: الحرمة ما لا يجوز انتهاكه ووجب رعايته

TABATABAI:22:29-30/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:29-30/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:22:29-30/r6.claim: ‘That’ summarizes the rites legislated for Abraham and later pilgrims: ihram, circumambulation, prayer, sacrifice sincerely for God, and avoidance of associating partners.
TABATABAI:22:29-30/r6.anchor: أي الأمر ذلك أي الذي شرعناه لإبراهيم عليه السلام ومن بعده من نسك الحج هو ذلك الذي ذكرناه

TABATABAI:22:29-30/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:29-30/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:22:29-30/r7.claim: Exalting God’s inviolable limits means refraining from crossing the boundaries He set and committing what lies beyond them.
TABATABAI:22:29-30/r7.anchor: وهي الأمور التي نهى عنها وضرب دونها حدودا منع عن تعديها واقتراف ما وراءها وتعظيمها الكف عن التجاوز إليها

TABATABAI:22:29-30/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:29-30/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:22:29-30/r8.claim: The sanctities sentence prepares for the permission of livestock with exceptions: although livestock are lawful provisions, the exception indicates that some carry a divine prohibition.
TABATABAI:22:29-30/r8.anchor: أن هذه الجملة توطئة وتمهيد لما بعدها

TABATABAI:22:29-30/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:29-30/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:22:29-30/r9.claim: ‘What is recited to you’ refers to prohibitions already being recited, not a future reference to the verse in al-Ma’idah; food prohibitions appeared in al-An‘am, al-Nahl, and al-Baqara, so a future reading is unnecessary.
TABATABAI:22:29-30/r9.anchor: استمرار التلاوة، فإن محرمات الأكل نزلت في سورة الأنعام

TABATABAI:22:29-30/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:29-30/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:22:29-30/r10.claim: Though carrion, blood, pork, and meat dedicated to other than God are all forbidden, the pilgrimage context especially targets pagan offerings to idols at the Ka‘ba, Safa, Marwa, and Mina.
TABATABAI:22:29-30/r10.anchor: إلا أن العناية في الآية بشهادة سياق ما قبلها وما بعدها بخصوص ما أهل به لغير الله

TABATABAI:22:30-32/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:30-32/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:22:30-32/r1.claim: The commands generally prohibit approaching idols and false speech used for idol worship in pilgrimage, including naming idols over sacrificial animals; the following fa makes this a consequence of the prior command to honor sanctities.
TABATABAI:22:30-32/r1.anchor: نهي عام عن التقرب إلى الأصنام وقول الباطل أورد لغرض التقرب إلى الأصنام في عمل الحج

TABATABAI:22:30-32/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:30-32/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:22:30-32/r2.claim: Calling the idols defilement signals the reason to avoid them; applying avoidance directly to the objects, rather than acts involving them, emphatically extends the prohibition.

TABATABAI:22:30-32/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:30-32/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:22:30-32/r3.claim: Min is explanatory: it identifies the defilement as idols; reading it as source or partitive, so that it means idol worship, strains and disrupts the straightforward sense.

TABATABAI:22:30-32/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:30-32/r4.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:22:30-32/r4.claim: Some take min as indicating origin: avoid the defilement that comes from idols, namely their worship; another group reads it partitivally as a defiling aspect of idols, namely worship. The author calls both readings strained.
TABATABAI:22:30-32/r4.anchor: وذكر بعضهم أنها ابتدائية والمعنى اجتنبوا الرجس الكائن من الأوثان وهو عبادتها

TABATABAI:22:30-32/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:30-32/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:22:30-32/r6.claim: ‘Hanifs for God’ and ‘not associating with Him’ are both circumstantial clauses describing those commanded to avoid idols and dedicate sacrifices to God; pagans’ pilgrimage chant contradicted this.
TABATABAI:22:30-32/r6.anchor: حال كونكم مائلين إليه ممن سواه غير مشركين به

TABRISI:22:29-30/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:29-30/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:22:29-30/r13.claim: Some place a pause at “that,” meaning this is how Hajj and its rites were prescribed.
TABRISI:22:29-30/r13.anchor: قيل ههنا وقف ومعناه الأمر ذلك أي هكذا أمر الحج والمناسك

TABRISI:22:29-30/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:29-30/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:22:29-30/r14.claim: Revering God’s inviolable things benefits a person with his Lord in the hereafter; they are things not to be violated.
TABRISI:22:29-30/r14.anchor: أي فالتعظيم خير له عند ربه أي في الآخرة والحرمة ما لا يحل انتهاكه

TABRISI:22:29-30/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:29-30/r15.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:22:29-30/r15.claim: Al-Zajjaj defines an inviolable duty as something to uphold and not neglect; here it is what God forbids, revered by avoiding it.
TABRISI:22:29-30/r15.anchor: وقال الزجاج: الحرمة ما وجب القيام به وحرم التفريط فيه

TABRISI:22:29-30/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:29-30/r16.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
TABRISI:22:29-30/r16.claim: Most exegetes understand the inviolable things here as the Hajj rites, as the surrounding verses indicate.
TABRISI:22:29-30/r16.anchor: واختار أكثر المفسرين في معنى الحرمات هنا أنها المناسك لدلالة ما يتصل بها من الآيات

TABRISI:22:29-30/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:29-30/r17.speaker: ابن زيد
TABRISI:22:29-30/r17.claim: Ibn Zayd identifies them as the Sacred House, territory, month, and Mosque, citing 2:194.
TABRISI:22:29-30/r17.anchor: وقيل: معناها ههنا البيت الحرام والبلد الحرام والشهر الحرام والمسجد الحرام عن ابن زيد

TABRISI:22:30/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:30/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:22:30/r1.claim: The citation to 2:194, “sacred things are subject to retaliation,” supports the preceding identification of sacred things.

TABRISI:22:30/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:30/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:22:30/r2.claim: The lawful livestock are camels, cattle, and sheep.

TABRISI:22:30/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:30/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:22:30/r3.claim: The exclusions are cases listed in Surat al-Maida, including carrion, strangled animals, and animals beaten to death.
TABRISI:22:30/r3.anchor: يعني في سورة المائدة من الميتة والمنخنقة والموقوذة ونحوها

TABRISI:22:30/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:30/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:22:30/r4.claim: Min is explanatory: avoid the filth that consists of idols.
TABRISI:22:30/r4.anchor: من هنا للتبيين والتقدير فاجتنبوا الرجس الذي هو الأوثان

TABRISI:22:30/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:30/r5.speaker: أصحابنا
TABRISI:22:30/r5.claim: Imami reports include chess, backgammon, and other gambling among the prohibited filth.
TABRISI:22:30/r5.anchor: وروى أصحابنا أن اللعب بالشطرنج والنرد وسائر أنواع القمار من ذلك

TABRISI:22:30/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:30/r6.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:22:30/r6.claim: Another explanation says polytheists smeared idols with sacrificial blood, so that blood was called filth.
TABRISI:22:30/r6.anchor: وقيل: إنهم كانوا يلطخون الأوثان بدماء قرابينهم فسمي ذلك رجسا

TABRISI:22:30/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:30/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:22:30/r7.claim: The command to avoid false speech means to avoid lying.

TABRISI:22:30/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:30/r8.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:22:30/r8.claim: Another view applies false speech to the polytheists’ talbiya, which names a partner supposedly owned by God along with what it owns.
TABRISI:22:30/r8.anchor: وقيل: هو تلبية المشركين لبيك لا شريك لك إلا شريكا هو لك تملكه وما ملك

TABRISI:22:30/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:30/r9.speaker: أصحابنا
TABRISI:22:30/r9.claim: Imami reports also include singing and distracting speech under the prohibition of false speech.
TABRISI:22:30/r9.anchor: وروى أصحابنا أنه يدخل فيه الغناء وسائر الأقوال الملهية

TABRISI:22:30/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:30/r10.speaker: أيمن بن خريم
TABRISI:22:30/r10.claim: Ayman ibn Khuraym reports that the Prophet equated false testimony with associating partners with God, then recited these commands to pair the prohibitions.
TABRISI:22:30/r10.anchor: وروى أيمن بن خريم عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قام خطيبا فقال

THALABI:v7p20/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p20/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p20/r4.claim: Glorifying God’s inviolable things means avoiding His disobedience, and that is better for a person before his Lord.
THALABI:v7p20/r4.anchor: ذلك ومن يعظم حرمات الله فيجتنب معاصيه فهو خير له عند ربه.

THALABI:v7p20/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p20/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
THALABI:v7p20/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd identifies the inviolable things as the Sacred Landmark, House, Mosque, and territory.
THALABI:v7p20/r5.anchor: قال ابن زيد: الحرمات: المشعر الحرام والبيت الحرام والمسجد الحرام والبلد الحرام

THALABI:v7p20/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p20/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p20/r6.claim: Another reported interpretation takes the inviolable things to be the pilgrimage rites.

THALABI:v7p20/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p20/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p20/r7.claim: Livestock may be eaten after proper slaughter except Qur’anic prohibitions, including carrion, blood, and animals over which God’s name was not invoked.
THALABI:v7p20/r7.anchor: وأحلت لكم الأنعام أن تأكلوها إذا ذكيتموها إلا ما يتلى عليكم في القرآن وهو قوله حرمت عليكم الميتة والدم الآية

THALABI:v7p20/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p20/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p20/r8.claim: Another view says livestock are lawful during ihram except game, which is forbidden in the sacred state.
THALABI:v7p20/r8.anchor: وقيل: وأحلت لكم الأنعام في حال إحرامكم إلا ما يتلى عليكم من الصيد فإنه حرام في حال الإحرام.

THALABI:v7p20/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p20/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p20/r9.claim: Avoiding the filth of idols means avoiding their worship, since idols themselves are filth.
THALABI:v7p20/r9.anchor: فاجتنبوا الرجس من الأوثان يعني عبادتها لأن الأوثان كلها رجس.

THALABI:v7p20/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p20/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p20/r10.claim: False speech means lying and slander.
THALABI:v7p20/r10.anchor: واجتنبوا قول الزور يعني الكذب والبهتان.

THALABI:v7p20/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p20/r11.speaker: أيمن بن حريم
THALABI:v7p20/r11.claim: Ayman ibn Khuraym reports that the Prophet equated false testimony with associating partners with God and recited this verse.
THALABI:v7p20/r11.anchor: قال أيمن بن حريم: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم خطيبا فقال: «يا أيها الناس عدلت شهادة الزور الشرك بالله، ثم قرأ هذه الآية»

THALABI:v7p20/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p20/r12.speaker: بعضهم
THALABI:v7p20/r12.claim: Some identify false speech as the polytheists’ talbiya, which adds a partner whom God owns along with all that partner owns.
THALABI:v7p20/r12.anchor: وقال بعضهم: هو قول المشركين في تلبيتهم: لبيك لا شريك لك إلا شريك هو لك، تملكه وما ملك.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p292#5/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p292#5/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p292#5/r1.claim: God's sacred rites include casting the pebbles, standing at Jamʿ, and similar rites.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p292#5/r1.anchor: ومن يعظم حرمات الله} يعني رمي الجمار، والوقوف بجمع، وأشباه ذلك. وهي شعائر الله.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p292#5/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p292#5/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p292#5/r2.claim: The prohibited livestock categories recited in al-Māʾida include carrion, animals killed by blows, falls, or goring.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p292#5/r2.anchor: وأحلت لكم الأنعام إلا ما يتلى عليكم} يعني في سورة المائدة من الميتة والموقوذة والمتردية والنطيحة (3) .

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p376#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p376#2/r1.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p376#2/r1.claim: Abu Ishaq parses ذلك as nominative, with an implied الأمر: the matter is thus.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p376#2/r1.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: موضع (ذلك) رفع. المعنى: الأمر ذلك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p376#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p376#2/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p376#2/r2.claim: The reference is to the Hajj practices just mentioned.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p376#2/r2.anchor: يعني ما ذكر من أعمال الحج.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p376#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p376#2/r3.speaker: الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p376#2/r3.claim: Al-Layth defines a hurma as something whose violation is forbidden; a person may be respected because of companionship or a right.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p376#2/r3.anchor: قال الليث: الحرمة ما لا يحل انتهاكه، وتقول: فلان له حرمة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p376#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p376#2/r4.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p376#2/r4.claim: Al-Zajjaj defines a hurma as something one must uphold and may not neglect.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p376#2/r4.anchor: وقال الزجاج: الحرمة: ما وجب القيام به وحرم التفريط فيه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p376#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p376#2/r5.speaker: عطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p376#2/r5.claim: Ata says the sacred limits here are God’s sins: prohibited things that must be left unviolated.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p376#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p376#2/r6.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p376#2/r6.claim: Mujahid includes Mecca, Hajj, Umra, and sins forbidden by God; the author says this combines commanded rites, which must not be neglected, and forbidden acts, which must not be committed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p376#2/r6.anchor: وقال مجاهد: الحرمة مكة والحج والعمرة، وما نهى الله عنه من معاصيه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p376#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p376#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p376#2/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas in Ata’s report says the phrase means God’s obligations and Sunna; the author prefers this as the most comprehensive account because it includes commands and prohibitions.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p376#2/r7.anchor: وقال ابن عباس في رواية عطاء: يريد فرائض الله عز وجل وسننه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p376#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p376#2/r8.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p376#2/r8.claim: Many commentators, including Abu Ishaq, focus on pilgrimage, Umra, and the other rites, while allowing that every divine obligation is a sacred limit because neglect is forbidden.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p376#2/r8.anchor: فقال أبو إسحاق: {حرمات الله}: الحج والعمرة وسائر المناسك. ثم قال: وكل ما فرضه الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p376#2/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p376#2/r9.speaker: ابن قتيبة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p376#2/r9.claim: Ibn Qutayba specifies stoning the pillars, standing at Muzdalifa, and similar rites; revering the rites means performing them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p376#2/r9.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة: يعني رمي (¬2) الجمار، والوقوف بجمع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p376#2/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p376#2/r10.speaker: ابن زيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p376#2/r10.claim: Ibn Zayd restricts the sacred limits to five: the Sacred House, territory, month, mosque, and ihram; the author links this to 2:194.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p376#2/r10.anchor: وخص ابن زيد الحرمات بما يقع عليه اسم الحرام، فقال: الحرمات: هي خمس: البيت الحرام

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p379/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p379/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p379/r1.claim: The pronoun فهو refers to the act of revering; a verb can signify its verbal noun, which the pronoun then resumes.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p379/r1.anchor: وقوله: {فهو} أي: التعظيم. والفعل يدل على المصدر، فكنى عنه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p379/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p379/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p379/r2.claim: Being better for him with his Lord means reward in the afterlife; Ibn Abbas describes it as an increase in obedience and fear of God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p379/r2.anchor: وقوله {خير له عند ربه} يعني في الآخرة. وقال ابن عباس: فإن ذلك زيادة له في طاعة الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p379/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p379/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p379/r3.claim: The permitted livestock are camels, cattle, and sheep, except the prohibitions recited in al-Maida, including carrion and animals strangled to death.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p379/r3.anchor: وقوله: {وأحلت لكم الأنعام} يعني: الإبل والبقر والغنم {إلا ما يتلى عليكم} أي: تحريمه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p379/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p379/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p379/r4.claim: Rijs means something foul or filthy, and every filthy thing is rijs; the discussion also appeared at 5:90 and 6:125.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p379/r4.anchor: الرجس: الشيء القذر. وكل قذر رجس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p379/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p379/r5.speaker: شمر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p379/r5.claim: Shammar says Arabs called any erected figure of wood, stone, gold, silver, copper, or similar material a wathan; Christians also set up and venerated the cross.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p379/r5.anchor: قال شمر: الأوثان عند العرب: كل تمثال من خشب أو حجارة أو ذهب أو فضة أو نحاس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p379/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p379/r6.speaker: الأعشى
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p379/r6.claim: Al-A‘sha calls the Christian cross a wathan in his poem, using the term for the object around which Christians worship.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p379/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p379/r7.speaker: النبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p379/r7.claim: In a report from Adi ibn Hatim, the Prophet calls the golden cross he wore a wathan and tells him to remove it; no grading is given.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p379/r7.anchor: وهو ما روي أن عدي بن حاتم قال: قدمت على النبي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p379/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p379/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p379/r8.claim: Wathan derives from the verb for standing firmly in place; wāthin means settled or stationary, and the poem describes keeping faith with old companions.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p379/r8.anchor: واشتقاق هذا اللفظ من قولهم: وثن الشيء، إذا قام في مكانه وثبت. والواثن: الشيء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p379/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p379/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p379/r9.claim: The command means to keep away from idols; Ibn Abbas glosses it specifically as avoiding their worship, which is rijs because it causes sin according to al-Kalbi.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p379/r9.anchor: والمعنى: كونوا على جانب من الأوثان فإنها رجس. قال ابن عباس: يريد عبادة الأوثان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p379/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p379/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p379/r10.claim: Ata’s report from Ibn Abbas and Ibn Zayd gloss rijs as punishment; al-Zajjaj says it is a curse in this world and punishment in the next.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p379/r10.anchor: وقال عطاء عن ابن عباس: الرجس: العذاب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p379/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p379/r11.speaker: رؤبة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p379/r11.claim: Ru’ba’s cited line uses الوثن for steadfastness in a bond; the author glosses it as remaining true to the old companionship.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p379/r11.anchor: قال رؤبة: على أخلاء الصفاء الوثن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p381/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p381/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p381/r1.claim: The explanations of rijs here repeat those given for 6:125.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p381/r1.anchor: وهذا الأقوال ذكروها في قوله: {كذلك يجعل الله الرجس}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p381/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p381/r2.speaker: الأخفش
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p381/r2.claim: Al-Akhfash takes rijs as the consequence arising from idols, namely their worship; worship is called rijs because it leads to curse and punishment, or, for al-Kalbi, because it is sin.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p381/r2.anchor: قال الأخفش في هذه الآية: المعنى: فاجتنبوا الرجس الذي يكون منها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p381/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p381/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p381/r3.claim: Abu Ishaq treats من as identifying a kind, so the sense is the rijs that is an idol; most exegetes take it as an explanatory مِن جنس.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p381/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p381/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p381/r4.claim: On this reading rijs means the idol itself, called rijs as idol worship is called rijs in the other reading; it does not mean physical dirt or repulsiveness.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p381/r4.anchor: وليس الرجس في هذه الآية من القذارة والاستقذار في شيء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p381/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p381/r5.speaker: المبرد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p381/r5.claim: Al-Mubarrad says all idols are rijs, so مِن associates the rijs with the noun rather than making it a part of the idols; he compares 48:29 and Sibawayh’s phrase about words of Arabic.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p381/r5.anchor: وقال المبرد: {فاجتنبوا الرجس من الأوثان} والأوثان كلها رجس، وتأويله -والله أعلم: فاجتنبوا الرجس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p383/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p383/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p383/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: {واجتنبوا قول الزور} الزور (¬2): الباطل والكذب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p383/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p383/r2.speaker: عطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p383/r2.claim: Some identify the false statement as associating partners with God, including the pagan talbiya that made an idol a partner; Ata from Ibn Abbas says it was their claim that angels were God’s daughters.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p383/r2.anchor: قال عطاء عن ابن عباس: يريد قولهم: الملائكة بنات الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p383/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p383/r3.speaker: النبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p383/r3.claim: Khuraym ibn Fatīk reports that the Prophet twice equated false testimony with associating partners, then recited this verse, pairing the bans on idol worship and false testimony.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p383/r3.anchor: وروى خريم بن فاتك (¬6): أن النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم- قام خطيبا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p383/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p383/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p383/r4.claim: The interpretation of false testimony as idolatrous speech is also attributed to Abdullah ibn Masud and Wa’il ibn Rabi‘a.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p383/r4.anchor: وهذا قول عبد الله بن مسعود (¬2)، ووائل بن ربيعة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p383/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p383/r5.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p383/r5.claim: Abu Ishaq says the verse also forbids inventing livestock taboos like those in 6:139 and the Bahira and Sa’iba; declaring something lawful or unlawful without warrant is lying against God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p383/r5.anchor: وذكر أبو إسحاق قولا آخر، فقال: الآية تدل على أنهم نهوا أن يحرموا

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:30-32/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:30-32/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:30-32/r1.claim: “That” points back to the matter just described.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:30-32/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:30-32/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:30-32/r2.claim: God's sacred ordinances are His obligations and established practices.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:30-32/r2.anchor: فرائض الله وسننه. { وأحلت لكم الأنعام } أن تأكلوها

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:30-32/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:30-32/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:30-32/r3.claim: Livestock may be eaten except for the animals prohibited in the cited passage, including carrion; the exception does not restore pre-Islamic bans such as bahira and saiba.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:30-32/r3.anchor: معنى هذا النهي تحريم ما حرمه أهل الجاهلية من البحيرة والسائبة وغير ذلك

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:30-32/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:30-32/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:30-32/r4.claim: Avoiding the impurity of idols means avoiding their worship.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:30-32/r4.anchor: يعني: عبادتها { واجتنبوا قول الزور } يعني: الشرك بالله

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:30-32/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:30-32/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:30-32/r5.claim: The false utterance to be avoided is associating partners with God.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:30-32/r5.anchor: يعني: الشرك بالله. { حنفاء لله } مسلمين عادلين عن كل دين سواه

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p369/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p369/r1.speaker: مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p369/r1.claim: Mujahid includes Mecca, pilgrimage, lesser pilgrimage, and all sins God has forbidden among His sacred limits.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p369/r1.anchor: تفسير مجاهد الحرمات: مكة، والحج، والعمرة، وما نهى الله عنه من معاصيه كلها

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p369/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p369/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p369/r2.claim: The exclusions recited in this verse are the forbidden foods listed in the Qur'an's dietary passage.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p369/r2.anchor: في سورة المائدة من: {الميتة والدم ولحم الخنزير وما أهل لغير الله به

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p369/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p369/r3.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p369/r3.claim: The author also links the rule to the prohibition on hunting while in ihram.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p369/r3.anchor: قال: {غير محلي الصيد وأنتم حرم} [المائدة: 1] وقد فسرت ذلك في المائدة

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p369/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p369/r4.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p369/r4.claim: Avoid idols because they are impure.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p369/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p369/r5.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p369/r5.claim: False speech means lying about God, that is, associating partners with Him.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p369/r5.anchor: وقول الزور: الكذب على الله يعني الشرك

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p369/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p369/r6.speaker: مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p369/r6.claim: Mujahid gives the broader gloss that false speech means lying.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p259/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p259/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p259/r1.claim: رجز means torment; Pharaoh's people use it for the affliction God lifts, and Satan's rجز is so called because his guile causes punishment.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p259/r1.anchor: الرجز: العذاب. قال الله تعالى- حكاية عن قوم فرعون:

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p259/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p259/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p259/r2.claim: رجس literally means stench or filth; unbelief and hypocrisy are called رجسا because they are foul.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p259/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p259/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p259/r3.claim: In the command to shun idols, الرجز denotes idols, named for the torment they bring about.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p259/r3.anchor: والرجز فاهجر (5) [المدثر: 5] ، يعني الأوثان، سماها رجزا-

ELMALILI:22:30/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:22:30/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:22:30/r1.claim: “That” sums up the preceding direction: this is the command and the way one must act.
ELMALILI:22:30/r1.anchor: İşte öyle yani emir böyle, böyle yapılmak lâzım gelir.

ELMALILI:22:30/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:22:30/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:22:30/r2.claim: God's sacred limits include His rulings, commands, and prohibitions, as well as places and things He has made sacred, such as the Sacred House, Mosque, town, sanctuary, and month.
ELMALILI:22:30/r2.anchor: Allah’ın ahkâmına, emirlerine, nehiylerine ve Beyt-i Haram

ELMALILI:22:30/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:22:30/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:22:30/r3.claim: Revering these limits means recognizing the duty to honor them and acting accordingly.
ELMALILI:22:30/r3.anchor: riayetin vücûbunu bilerek ve mûcebince amel ederek ihtiram ederse

ELMALILI:22:30/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:22:30/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:22:30/r4.claim: The worshipper will see the benefit of this reverence in the Hereafter with the Lord.

ELMALILI:22:30/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:22:30/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:22:30/r5.claim: Livestock are lawful and are not among the sacredly prohibited; the customary categories of bahira, saiba, wasila, and ham do not change that, and all eight pairs are lawful.
ELMALILI:22:30/r5.anchor: hurumâttan değildir. Sûre-i En‘âm’da beyan olunduğu üzere bahîre, sâibe, vasîle, hâm yok, semâniyete ezvâc hepsi helâl

ELMALILI:22:30/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:22:30/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:22:30/r6.claim: The exception is the forbidden food detailed at 5:3: carrion, blood, swine, and animals dedicated to other than God.
ELMALILI:22:30/r6.anchor: meyte, dem, hınzır[^2], وَمَٓا اُهِلَّ لِغَيْرِ اللهِّٰ’dır [5/3]

ELMALILI:22:30/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:22:30/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:22:30/r7.claim: Avoid both tangible filth such as carrion and the spiritual filth of idols; slaughter livestock in God's name and cleanse the House of idols.
ELMALILI:22:30/r7.anchor: meyte gibi hissî ve maddî pisliklerden ictinab ile beraber nusub u asnâm gibi mânevî pisliklerden de sakınınız

ELMALILI:22:30/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:22:30/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:22:30/r8.claim: Avoid false speech: do not tell lies or promote them, and keep away from falsification.
ELMALILI:22:30/r8.anchor: söylemediğiniz gibi tervic de etmeyiniz, tezvîrâttan uzak olunuz.

ELMALILI:22:30/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:22:30/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:22:30/r9.claim: Idol worship is itself a form of falsification akin to false testimony, and indeed its chief form.
ELMALILI:22:30/r9.anchor: evsâna tapmak da yalancı şâhidlik kabîlinden tezvîrâttır, hatta tezvîrâtın başıdır.

ELMALILI:22:30/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:22:30/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:22:30/r10.claim: It is false speech and belief to declare forbidden what God did not forbid, including claims that bahira, saiba, wasila, and ham are prohibited; such filth must be shunned.
ELMALILI:22:30/r10.anchor: Allah’ın haram kılmadığı şeylere haram demekten; “bahîre, sâibe, vasîle, hâm haramdır” demek gibi yalan sözlerden ve akidelerden sakının

BURHAN:v4p418/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p418/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p418/r1.claim: In the phrase about avoiding the impurity of idols, “min” may explain the genus or be partitive; the text then reports a disagreement over these parses.
BURHAN:v4p418/r1.anchor: الشاهد في غير الأولى فإن تلك للابتداء

BURHAN:v4p418/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p418/r2.speaker: متأخري المغاربة
BURHAN:v4p418/r2.claim: Later Maghribi grammarians reject an explanatory “min” here: it marks the starting point of the category of idols, since impurity is broader than idols.
BURHAN:v4p418/r2.anchor: وقد انكر القوم من متأخري المغاربة بيان الجنس وقالوا هي في الآية الشريفة لابتداء الغاية

BURHAN:v4p418/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p418/r3.speaker: ابن أبي الربيع
BURHAN:v4p418/r3.claim: Ibn Abi al-Rabiʿ prefers the partitive reading: the impurity deriving from idols is worshipping them, supported by 39:17.
BURHAN:v4p418/r3.anchor: وقيل للتبعيض لأن الرجس منها هو عبادتها واختاره ابن أبي الربيع

BURHAN:v4p416/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p416/r3.speaker: التراس
BURHAN:v4p416/r3.claim: Al-Tarras is cited for saying min never separates from its explanatory-gender function; this use can be identified by substitution with alladhi and adjectival syntax.
BURHAN:v4p416/r3.anchor: وقيل إنها لا تنفك عنه مطلقا حكاه التراس ولها علامتان إن يصح وضع الذي موضعها

BURHAN:v4p416/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p416/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p416/r4.claim: Explanatory min specifies which kind of ambiguous impurity is meant: idols; other impurities are excluded by separate evidence, and idols are part of impurity.
BURHAN:v4p416/r4.anchor: وغيرها فلما اقتصر عليه لم يعلم المراد فلما صرح بذكر الأوثان علم أنها المراد من الجنس

ITQAN:v4p522#3/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p522#3/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ITQAN:v4p522#3/r1.claim: Yaʿlā b. Umayya reports the Prophet saying that hoarding food in Mecca is illicit deviation.
ITQAN:v4p522#3/r1.anchor: أخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن يعلى بن أمية أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

ITQAN:v4p522#3/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p522#3/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ITQAN:v4p522#3/r2.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr reports a ḥasan hadith that the Kaʿba is called the Ancient House because no tyrant has ever overcome it.
ITQAN:v4p522#3/r2.anchor: وأخرج الترمذي وحسنه عن ابن الزبير قال قال رسول الله

ITQAN:v4p522#3/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p522#3/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ITQAN:v4p522#3/r3.claim: Khuraym b. Fātik reports the Prophet equating false testimony with associating partners with God and then reciting the verse's command to avoid idolatry and false speech.
ITQAN:v4p522#3/r3.anchor: وأخرج أحمد عن خريم بن فاتك الأسدي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

ITQAN:v4p406/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p406/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ITQAN:v4p406/r1.claim: A report from ʿAlī says whoever memorizes the Qur'an and treats its lawful and forbidden rules accordingly enters Paradise and intercedes for ten condemned relatives.
ITQAN:v4p406/r1.anchor: وأخرج الترمذي وابن ماجه وأحمد من حديث علي ( من قرأ القرآن فاستظهره فأحل حلاله

ITQAN:v4p406/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p406/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ITQAN:v4p406/r2.claim: Abū Umāma reports that a verse learned from God's book will meet its learner on Resurrection day smiling at him.
ITQAN:v4p406/r2.anchor: وأخرج الطبراني من حديث أبي أمامة ( من تعلم آية من كتاب الله استقبلته يوم القيامة

ITQAN:v4p406/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p406/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ITQAN:v4p406/r3.claim: ʿĀʾisha reports in the Ṣaḥīḥayn that a skilled reciter is with the noble angels, while one who struggles and stammers earns two rewards.
ITQAN:v4p406/r3.anchor: وأخرج الشيخان وغيرهما من حديث عائشة ( الماهر بالقرآن مع السفرة الكرام والبررة

ITQAN:v4p406/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p406/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ITQAN:v4p406/r4.claim: Jābir reports that a person who has memorized the Qur'an has an answered supplication with God, granted in this life or kept for the next.
ITQAN:v4p406/r4.anchor: وأخرج الطبراني في الأوسط من حديث جابر ( من جمع القرآن كانت له عند الله دعوة مستجابة

ITQAN:v4p406/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p406/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ITQAN:v4p406/r5.claim: Abū Mūsā reports a parable comparing the believing reader to a citron, the believing nonreader to a date, the sinful reader to basil and the sinful nonreader to colocynth.
ITQAN:v4p406/r5.anchor: وأخرج الشيخان من حديث أبي موسى ( مثل المؤمن الذي يقرأ القرآن مثل الأترجة طعمها طيب

ITQAN:v4p406/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p406/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ITQAN:v4p406/r6.claim: ʿUthmān reports that the best people learn and teach the Qur'an; al-Bayhaqī adds that the Qur'an surpasses all speech as God surpasses creation.
ITQAN:v4p406/r6.anchor: وأخرج الشيخان من حديث عثمان ( خيركم وفي لفظ إن أفضلكم من تعلم القرآن وعلمه

ITQAN:v4p406/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p406/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ITQAN:v4p406/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that a person whose heart holds nothing from the Qur'an is like a ruined house.
ITQAN:v4p406/r7.anchor: وأخرج الترمذي والحاكم من حديث ابن عباس ( إن الذي ليس في جوفه شيء من القرآن كالبيت الخرب

ITQAN:v4p406/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p406/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ITQAN:v4p406/r8.claim: Abū Dharr reports that learning one Qur'anic verse is better than performing one hundred cycles of prayer.
ITQAN:v4p406/r8.anchor: وأخرج ابن ماجه من حديث أبي ذر ( لأن تغدو فتتعلم آية من كتاب الله خير لك من أن تصلي

ITQAN:v4p406/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p406/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ITQAN:v4p406/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that learning and following the Qur'an guides a person from error and protects him from the evil of the final reckoning.
ITQAN:v4p406/r9.anchor: وأخرج الطبراني من حديث ابن عباس ( من تعلم كتاب الله ثم اتبع ما فيه هداه الله به

ITQAN:v4p406/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p406/r10.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ITQAN:v4p406/r10.claim: Abū Shurayḥ al-Khuzāʿī reports that the Qur'an is a rope with one end held by God and one by people; holding it prevents straying and destruction.
ITQAN:v4p406/r10.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي شيبة من حديث أبي شريح الخزاعي ( أن هذا القرآن سبب طرفه بيد الله وطرفه بأيديكم

ITQAN:v4p406/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p406/r11.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ITQAN:v4p406/r11.claim: ʿAlī reports that the bearers of the Qur'an are in God's shade on the day when no other shade exists.
ITQAN:v4p406/r11.anchor: وأخرج الديلمي من حديث علي ( حملة القرآن في ظل الله يوم لا ظل إلا ظله

NAHHAS:v3p95/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p95/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p95/r3.claim: ذلك refers to the foregoing duties and prescriptions.
NAHHAS:v3p95/r3.anchor: أي الأمر ذلك من الفروض والمعنى ومن يعظم عنده فعل الحرام

NAHHAS:v3p95/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p95/r4.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p95/r4.claim: To honor God’s prohibitions is to treat forbidden acts with reverence for God and fear of Him; doing so is better for the person before his Lord.
NAHHAS:v3p95/r4.anchor: المعنى ومن يعظم عنده فعل الحرام تعظيما لله جل وعز وخوفا منه ( فهو خير له )

NAHHAS:v3p95/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p95/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p95/r5.claim: هو خير له is a subject with its predicate.
NAHHAS:v3p95/r5.anchor: ومن يعظم عنده فعل الحرام تعظيما لله جل وعز وخوفا منه ( فهو خير له ) ابتداء وخبر

NAHHAS:v3p95/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p95/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p95/r6.claim: The exception in إلا ما يتلى عليكم is accusative.

NAHHAS:v3p95/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p95/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p95/r7.claim: Grammarians take من as a specification of kind; al-Akhfash instead takes it partitivally, meaning avoid the idolatrous abomination, namely worship of idols, a rare but good analysis.
NAHHAS:v3p95/r7.anchor: ( من ) عند النحويين لبيان الجنس إلا أن الأخفش زعم أنها للتبعيض أي فاجتنبوا الرجس الذي هو من الأوثان

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p148/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p148/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p148/r1.claim: An ideal brother or friend can be evoked through imagined qualities without referring to a known person; the source illustrates this with poetic wishes and al-Ma'mun's offer to trade the caliphate for such a companion.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p148/r1.anchor: على أنك قدرت إنسانا هذه صفته ، وهذا شأنه ، وأحلت السامع على ما يعن في الوهم دون أن يكون قد عرف رجلا بهذه الصفة

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p148/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p148/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p148/r2.claim: 'Zayd is the one who departed' resolves uncertainty about who performed a known departure; 'the one departing is Zayd' identifies a person seen at a distance.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p148/r2.anchor: فإذا قلت : زيد المنطلق ، أزلت عنك الشك ، وجعلته يقطع وبأنه كان من زيد

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p148/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p148/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p148/r3.claim: Fronting an active participle or attribute makes it identify its bearer rather than assert a quality already visible, as when brocade identifies a familiar person.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p148/r3.anchor: فمتى رأيت اسم فاعل أو صفة من الصفات قد بدىء به فجعل مبتدأ ، وجعل الذي هو صاحب الصفة في المعنى خبرا فاعلم

DAMGHANI:v1p123/r10.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p123/r10.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p123/r10.claim: Ḥurumāt Allāh means the rites of pilgrimage.
DAMGHANI:v1p123/r10.anchor: فوجه منهما : الحرمات المناسك قوله تعالى في سورة الحج

BURHAN:v3p334/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p334/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p334/r8.claim: The final category shown shifts from past tense to command, as in قل أمر ربي بالقسط followed by وأقيموا, and the command after أحلت لكم الأنعام.
